sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Which five checks and steps make up starting your vehicle in Kentucky?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Starting means consulting the owner's manual, braking with the right foot, confirming park, keying on, and scanning fuel, ABS, and bag gauges.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: How should your shifter, eyes, blinker, and right heel work together when pulling away from a stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Moving means shifting to drive under braking, checking front, sides, and rear, signaling, then easing onto the accelerator with heel down and foot-top on the pedal.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What three-step habit brings your car to a smooth, safe everyday stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Stopping means mirror-checking the rear, swapping to the brake, and pressing steadily to a halt.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Whether moving forward or backing in reverse, which direction do you turn the steering wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: The wheel always turns toward the intended travel direction, forward or reverse.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Where does the vehicle-starting chain finish compared with the moving-off chain?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Starting chains brake, park, key, and gauges, while moving chains brake, drive, checks, signal, and throttle.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How do foot braking and steering direction pair up across normal stops and maneuvers?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Stopping swaps feet to steady braking, while steering always points where the car should go.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Why did driver training retire the old ten-and-two steering-wheel hand placement?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Two-and-ten hand placement is retired as airbag-dangerous.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Where and how should your fingers, thumbs, and palms hold the steering wheel today?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Hands grip the wheel's outside at three and nine with firm gentle fingers and raised thumbs, never from the inside or by the palms.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Which clock-face hand position is retired for airbag safety, and which outside grip replaces it?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Two-and-ten is retired as airbag-dangerous, while three-and-nine outside grips with raised thumbs rule today.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What outside check should open every backing maneuver, and why isn't sitting in the driver's seat enough?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Backing starts with a walk-around look since children and small objects hide from the seat.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: How should your foot, both hands, and eyes be positioned when backing straight?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Reverse posture means braking into gear, left hand at twelve, right arm over the seatback, and eyes through the rear glass.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Why can't you rely solely on mirrors while backing up?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Mirrors aid backing but miss the zone directly behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How fast should you roll in reverse, and how big should steering inputs be?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Reverse driving stays slow and gentle with slight steering toward the tail's path.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What extra glances do turning reverses require, and how long must your main gaze stay rearward?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.memory_hook: Quick front-side checks; rear-gaze until stopped
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Turning reverses add quick front-side checks, and rear gaze holds until fully stopped.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does a pre-backing walk-around complement what your mirrors can see?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Backing opens with a walk-around look for hidden children, while mirrors cover only what sits beyond the bumper zone.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does your stationary reverse setup pair with your moving reverse technique?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Reverse posture plants hands and eyes rearward, while reverse motion stays slow with slight steering and front-side checks.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Why must safe drivers keep their eyes moving in every direction instead of staring at one spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Safe driving opens with a fixed visual search in every direction, since spotting trouble early buys time to adjust speed or position, so keep your eyes roaming and never stare.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How far ahead should your forward scan reach, and why shouldn't you tuck close behind tall trucks?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Aim your gaze down your path to read the road, its users, and its conditions in time for calm decisions, ideally scanning twenty to thirty seconds ahead and refusing to tuck behind tall vehicles that steal your view.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Before which four everyday maneuvers must you sweep your mirrors to check traffic behind?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Sweep the sides for crossers and the mirrors for trailers, with rear checks mandatory before lane changes, slowdowns, stops, and intersection entries.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Along with matching road conditions and keeping a safe gap, how often should you check your speedometer?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Manage speed for roads and traffic, keep a real following gap, obey posted limits, and glance at the speedometer about once a minute.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What are Kentucky's four unposted default speeds across interstates, state highways, business-residential streets, and public parking lots?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Unposted Kentucky limits run sixty-five miles per hour on interstates and parkways, fifty-five miles per hour on other state highways, thirty-five miles per hour in business and residential districts, fifteen miles per hour in public-use off-street lots, with the transportation secretary able to raise select highways to seventy miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What caps nighttime speed, and what legal maximum applies when fog, snow, or rain cuts visibility to one hundred feet?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Never outdrive your headlights at night, and when heavy rain, snow, or fog cuts sight to one hundred feet, cap speed at twenty-five miles per hour on low beams.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: How should you approach overgrown corners and enter blind hills or curves?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Creep past intersection greenery, parked cars, signs, and buildings that hide side traffic, and enter hills and curves slow enough to halt for a stalled or crawling vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How do your twenty-to-thirty-second forward gaze and your side-and-mirror sweeps divide scanning jobs?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Far vision reads twenty to thirty seconds down your path, while side and mirror sweeps guard crossers and trailers.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How do Kentucky's unposted highway limits step down once you enter town districts and public lots?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.memory_hook: Sixty-five-fifty-five open; thirty-five town; fifteen lot
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Open-road defaults run sixty-five and fifty-five miles per hour, while settled areas drop to thirty-five and lots to fifteen.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Compare the speed rule for clear nighttime driving with heavy weather under one hundred feet of sight?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Darkness caps speed at headlight range, while one hundred-foot storms cap it at twenty-five miles per hour on low beams.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: When should you finish braking for a curve, and why avoid hard mid-curve braking?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Slow before every curve to a pace that carries slight steady throttle throughout, slowing further for weak grip, followers, and blind exits, since hard mid-curve braking breaks traction.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: On wet or icy roads, how does braking technique differ without anti-lock brakes versus with them?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Ease off at the first rain, snow, sleet, or ice, because slick rubber stops longer, turns wider, and skids or floats at speed or downhill, so postpone sharp braking and turning until grip returns, pumping gently without anti-lock brakes and pressing steadily with them.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What happens during hydroplaning, and how should you treat deep standing water across a roadway?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Hydroplaning floats steering tires onto pooled water like skis with zero road contact, so slow down on wet roads, keep tires firm and treaded, and never drive through large standing water but reroute instead.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What span does total stopping distance cover, and how long does alert perception time average?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Total stopping distance spans realization to rest under ideal conditions, grows with speed, and starts with perception time averaging three quarters second to one second in alert drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How long does foot-reaction time average, and roughly how far is pure braking distance from fifty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Reaction time from gas to brake averages three quarters second to one second, and braking distance from pedal to rest runs about one hundred fifty-eight feet from fifty miles per hour on dry pavement with sound brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Where does speed scrubbing belong on a winding road so tires hold cornering traction?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Curves want braking done before entry, while mid-curve stomps break traction.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How do your right-foot motions reverse between standard brakes and anti-lock brakes on slick pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Plain brakes pump gently on slick roads, while anti-lock brakes take one steady press.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How does smart driving on ordinary wet asphalt differ from meeting deep pooled water?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Wet roads want slower speeds and sound tread, while flooded roads want a different route entirely.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How does perception time fit inside total stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Total stopping distance spans realization to rest, while perception time covers only the recognition slice.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How do reaction time and fifty-mile-per-hour dry braking distance split the physical stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Reaction time moves the foot in three quarters second to one second, while braking distance then spends about one hundred fifty-eight feet from fifty miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What safety asset does keeping an open space cushion on all four sides buy you?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: A space cushion in every direction buys reaction time, so guard open room around your car at all times.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Which collision type leads crash statistics, and what minimum following gap does Kentucky's manual set?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Rear-enders top the crash list because tailgating blinds and starves reaction, so keep at least four seconds to the leader, since unreasonably tight following breaks the law.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: How do you measure Kentucky's minimum following cushion using a roadside landmark?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Time your gap by counting one-thousand-one through one-thousand-four from the leader's passing of a fixed point, slowing and recounting until you trail by no less than four seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: Under which five road, weather, or lead-vehicle situations must you stretch past four seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Stretch the gap on slick roads, behind big rigs, buses, campers, and trailers, at night and in foul weather, behind railroad-stopping buses and hazmat haulers, and behind quick-jinking motorcycles.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: How should you help when a trailing vehicle pulls out to overtake and merge ahead of you?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: When a follower wants past, ease off the gas and slow as needed so the passer gains room to slip in ahead of you.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: How should you manage side cushions, other drivers' blind spots, and oncoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Hold side room for lateral escapes where others can see you, shun lingering in blind spots by speeding up or dropping back, and give oncoming traffic its full half.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: How do you pad freeway mergers, walkers, wide trucks, parked doors, and interstate shoulder parkers?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.memory_hook: Make room; shift left past shoulders
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Open space for freeway mergers by shifting or slowing, pad pedestrians, children, and cyclists, slide outside for tractor-trailers, gap parked cars against doors and pull-outs, and on interstates swing left early past shoulder parkers before returning right.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Which three smooth habits protect your rear bumper when someone tailgates behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Steady speed, early signals, and extra nose room before slowing or turning help tailgaters hold off and buy you reaction time.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: Which four defensive responses let you absorb another driver's mistake before metal meets?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Cover others' mistakes by speeding, slowing, swerving, or stopping as the moment demands so the crash never happens.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How does Kentucky's dry-daylight following count compare with bad-weather or special-vehicle following?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Normal gaps hold four seconds by the thousand-count, while slick, dark, heavy, and twitchy company demands more.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Compare how you clear a neighbor's blind spot versus how you defuse a tailgater on your bumper?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Blind spots want you gone by speeding or dropping back, while your own tailgater wants steady speed and early signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: What risky reverse move should you avoid into live streets, and who can assist tight backing?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Back with extra care for the blind rear, shunning reverse entries into traffic and borrowing a ground guide when you can.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: What is the only legal move after rolling past your intended interstate exit?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Past your interstate exit, never back up or spin around; roll on to the next exit and circle back.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: What two goals define effective driver communication on the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Communication means broadcasting your place and plans while keeping your car conspicuous to all.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: Between what sunset-to-sunrise clock times—and during what visibility moments—must Kentucky headlamps shine?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Light headlamps from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, plus rainy, snowy, foggy, and dusky spells, sun-glare runs, and any moment others look dim, since dim-to-you means dim-to-them.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: When is a light horn tap helpful, and near whom is honking strictly forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Tap the horn lightly for lane-drifting walkers and cyclists, cutters-off mid-pass, and drifting or blind drivers, reserving the horn for real messages since blasts startle and anger, and never honk near blind pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: Beyond corner turns and lane changes, which other lateral moves and slowdowns require signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Signal before every direction change and slowdown, covering lane moves, passes, turns, merges, turnabouts, freeway entries and exits, curb departures, and roadside stops.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Must you signal on empty roads, do signals grant right-of-way, and are arm hand-signals legal in Kentucky?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Signal every single time even when the road looks empty, because the unseen car kills, checking blind spots over your shoulder, remembering signals grant no right-of-way, cancelling promptly, and using mechanical signals only since hand signals are banned.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Why should your turn blinker come on before your foot touches the brake for a mid-block driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Brake lights voice your slowdown, so signal before slowing for turn-offs lacking their own lanes and for parking or turning ahead of intersections.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: How does acceptable backing help in a tight lot contrast with missing a highway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Ordinary backing borrows a ground guide, while a missed interstate exit forbids backing altogether.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Where does Kentucky draw the line between helpful horn communication and prohibited honking?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: Light taps warn drifters and cutters, while blasts near blind pedestrians and anger-honks stay banned.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Summarize Kentucky's four rules on when signals run, what they grant, what type is legal, and afterward?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.memory_hook: Before moves, zero priority, mechanical, cancel
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: Signals precede every move and slowdown, yet grant no right-of-way and must be mechanical, prompt, and cancelled.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: How must drivers yield and adjust speed around crosswalks, intersections, neighborhoods, and flashing school zones?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Everyone owns the road together, so drive courteously and telegraph yourself; stay yield-ready for walkers anywhere, always yield in crosswalks marked or not including signed mid-block ones and to every pedestrian in the intersection even on green, brace for walkers on red turns, crawl past parked rows that hide crossers, scan before backing especially amid crowds, dip under the limit and coil to stop around playgrounds and homes, obey slower school limits when lights flash or children show and halt for patrol signals, while mid-road jaywalkers owe you the yield.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Where must you stop for a blind pedestrian with a cane or guide dog, and what fine applies?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Kentucky law yields the road to blind walkers with visible white canes or assistance dogs under a two hundred fifty dollars fine, so halt within five feet of the crosswalk short of advance bars to stay audible, and mind silent electrics and hybrids.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Which actions must you avoid around a blind pedestrian, and what cue says you may proceed?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Never talk a blind crosser across since they read traffic sound, never wait them out forever, roll when they step back and pocket the cane, never plug the crosswalk and force a traffic detour, and never honk at their confusion and fright.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does your duty toward pedestrians anywhere compare with walkers in crosswalks and intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Walkers anywhere earn readiness, while crosswalk and intersection walkers command the yield.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does Kentucky's penalty for failing to yield to white-cane or guide-dog walkers stand apart?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Ordinary walkers earn caution, while white-cane and guide-dog walkers command legal yield under a two hundred fifty dollars fine.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How should you behave while a blind walker decides, and what gesture clears you to drive?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Silent patience serves blind crossers, while step-back plus pocketed cane means roll.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: How does Kentucky traffic law classify bicycles, and what mistakes do novice riders often make?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Bicycles count as vehicles with matching rules, rights, and duties, so respect them, spot their faint profiles, and brace for novices who wobble, blow signs, and ride dark.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Where must drivers yield to cyclists, and under what five exceptions may cars enter bike lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Yield to bikes in intersections and where paths and lanes cross roads, and keep cars out of bike lanes except for alleys, driveways, official duty, police orders, and true emergencies.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: How should motorists handle speed, turns, horns, and slick surfaces when driving near cyclists?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Grant cyclists maximum room at low speed, let them clear before you turn, shun sudden slows that overmatch bike brakes, honk only to avert impact, watch lane entries and sidewalk kids, never slice or squeeze them off, expect wrong-way riders, and double care on wet, sandy, or gravelly skin.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: How and over what minimum distance must non-motor vehicles signal before making a turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Non-motor vehicles signal by hand, lamp, or device, flashing intermittently through the last fifty feet before the turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Why might a cyclist skip hand signals, and when must parked drivers scan for bikes?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Cyclists owe hand signals for turns and stops but may grip both bars in trouble, so read head and shoulder tells, door-check for riders before swinging out, and bike-check before backing near schools and homes.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: How much minimum side clearance and merge space must you give when passing a bicycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Pass bikes slowly with maximum room paced to their speed, holding at least three feet and returning right only when well clear, while honoring local bike ordinances.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Which five narrow situations allow a motor vehicle to cross or enter a bike lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Bike lanes ban cars outright, excepting alleys, driveways, duty, orders, and emergencies.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Why are abrupt brake checks and surprise horn blasts dangerous around bicycle riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Sudden slows overmatch bike brakes, while surprise honks swerve riders into harm.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: When may a cyclist keep both hands on the bars instead of signaling, and what warns you?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.memory_hook: Rough spots grab bars, watch heads
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Cyclists owe hand signals, yet may grip both bars, so read their head tells.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Which highways bar bicycles, and how must cyclists ride regarding traffic flow and signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Cyclists shun interstates and parkways, hand-signal, obey every control with full stops, hold posted or reasonable speed, and ride right with traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What night lamps, walker rules, and sidewalk or path rules apply to bicycle riders?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Cyclists yield crosswalks and sidewalks to walkers with a bell or horn warning, light white front and red rear at night, hug the right edge as slow traffic with extreme care when centering for debris, passes, or lefts, never ride sidewalks, never block walkers with parked bikes, and take adjacent paths when built.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: How many people may a bicycle carry, and how many riders may travel side by side?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Bikes carry only their designed souls and ride at most two abreast without fouling traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: What weight, top speed, and minimum rider age define legal electric scooters on Kentucky roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Electric scooters weigh under one hundred pounds on wheels with bars and a real brake, carry standers or sitters by motor, muscle, or both up to twenty miles per hour, admit riders sixteen and older to roads, lanes, and paths, and obey bike law with bike-grade motorist care.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: During which hours must electric scooters run front and rear lights, and how may they park?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.memory_hook: Half-hour dusk to dawn, clear walks
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Scooters burn at least one headlamp and one red tail from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise and in dim times, may sidewalk-park without blocking walkers, and obey every local ordinance.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: How do a cyclist's legal duties on roadways combine with duties toward pedestrians and darkness?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Cyclists obey drivers' controls on roads, yet yield sidewalks to walkers and light up at night.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: What rider age minimum and nighttime lighting window govern electric scooters in Kentucky?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Scooters admit riders sixteen and older, yet demand lamps from dusk-half-hour to dawn-half-hour.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: How much lane width and dry-road following gap must you give a motorcycle ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Motorcycles share full road rights and duties yet hide easily, so grant a whole lane always, sweep mirrors and blind spots, study fronts and flanks before lefts, distrust sticky signals until the turn proves real, and trail by four seconds or more, longer when wet.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Why do motorcyclists dart suddenly within their lane, and how fast do mopeds typically move?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Riders jink for potholes, gravel, slicks, seams, rails, and grooves that kill bikers, while scooters and mopeds crawl far below motorcycle pace.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Roughly how many car-truck crashes happen yearly, and what four traits set big rigs apart?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Over two hundred fifty thousand car-commercial crashes strike yearly yet mostly avoidably, since big rigs dwarf cars in size, blind spots, stopping and rolling distances, and turning girth.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Which side of a tractor-trailer hides the largest blind spot, and what mirror check saves you?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Side no-zones swallow cars beside tractors and buses, worst on the right from behind the cab down the trailer length, so trade mirror-face sightlines and shun lingering alongside where swerves kill.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: How far behind a large truck does its rear blind zone stretch, and how do hills affect rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Rear no-zones blind trucks to two hundred feet behind, so follow loose and mirror-visible with an escape in mind, while grades pin trucks near thirty-five miles per hour in the right lane, which you should vacate near hills and weigh stations.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: Why do trucks swing left before turning right, and where must you stop at intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Honor truck turn signals with wide berth since right turns swing left first, never wedge between rig and curb, wait out the whole turn, meet head-ons hugging far right against sideswipe and shove, turn left only when the rig's speed reads certain, and stop behind set-back lines that bank swing room.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: What rules protect you around trucks at exits, runaway ramps, uphill queues, and rail crossings?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Never cut rigs off for exits, turns, or single-lane zones, dodge mountain runaways and shun their escape ramps except as a doomed trucker, queue uphill left and visible with rollback room, dodge weigh-station right lanes, and avoid hazmat haulers that halt at every rail crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: What lane share and time cushion belong to every motorcycle in dry versus wet weather?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Motorcycles claim whole lanes, plus four-second trails stretching longer when wet.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Which dangerous driver habits get punished inside a truck's side no-zones versus its front no-zone?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Side zones punish lingerers beside trailers, while front zones punish divers ahead of them.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: How many feet of truck braking room sit ahead versus rear blind-spot length behind?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.memory_hook: Three thirty-five front, two hundred rear
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Front zones measure three hundred thirty-five feet of braking, while rear zones reach two hundred feet of blindness.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: How do turning trucks and oncoming cars share tight space when a rig turns right?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.memory_hook: Rigs swing wide, cars hug right
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Trucks swing left to turn right, while meeting cars hug far right.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: Why must passenger cars never cut off heavy trucks or stop near mountain escape ramps?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: Cutting rigs off courts death, while escape ramps serve doomed trucks alone.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: How must you respond whenever a vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights or sirens?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Siren-and-light rigs own the road, so yield to the edge without plugging intersections for anything flashing red or blue or sounding a siren.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Where must you hold during an emergency pass, and how close may you follow afterward?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.memory_hook: Curbside stop, stay five hundred back
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: At red-blue flashes or siren wails, dive immediately right or curbside clear of intersections and freeze until the emergency passes unless police or fire wave you on, and never tail emergency iron within five hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What calm steps should you take right after pulling over for a police traffic stop?

sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Kentucky belts every occupant of post-nineteen eighty-one vehicles in proper restraints, since belts beat ejection and hold control.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: Can Kentucky police pull you over solely for an unbuckled seat belt, and how must shoulder and lap straps sit?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Belt law is primary and stoppable, with shoulder straps across chest never under arms and lap belts snug low on hips.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: How fast do airbags fire in moderate-to-severe crashes, what harmless puff appears, and why must belts stay buckled?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Bags supplement belts in moderate-to-severe crashes, firing in a twentieth of a second with a powder puff, so belts stay on always.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: To stay safe around airbags, where belong your seat, hands, dashboard items, and children aged 12 and under?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.memory_hook: Slide back, clear dash, kids rear
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Seats slide fully back with hands off the wheel's center, nothing on the dash, and children twelve and under belted behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: May a rear-facing infant seat ever sit in front of an active passenger airbag, and how may one be turned off?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Rear-facing seats never face live passenger bags, switched off only by factory controls, per the owner's manual.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does a seat belt's protection across maneuvers and multi-hit crashes differ from an airbag's?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Belts restrain through every stop and turn, while bags fire once in a twentieth of a second as backup.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Which children by height must ride in a federally approved child restraint, and what fine-plus-fee hits violators?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Children forty inches or shorter ride in federal restraints on pain of a fifty dollars fine plus a ten dollars brain-injury fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What age and height range requires a booster seat in Kentucky, and what height graduates out regardless of age?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Under-eight riders between forty and fifty-seven inches use boosters, and anyone taller than fifty-seven inches skips them.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Where is the safest spot to anchor a child seat, who checks installations free, and what unattended-child crime applies under age 8?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.memory_hook: Center rear, troopers check, never leave
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Anchor a child safety seat securely, ideally in the middle rear position; a local State Police inspection site can help with installation. Leaving a child younger than eight in a vehicle is illegal under the stated rule when extreme indifference to human life creates a grave risk and causes the child to die.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: How does Kentucky's height cutoff for a full child safety restraint separate from its booster-seat band?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Forty inches and under means a full restraint, while forty to fifty-seven under age eight means a booster.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Under Kentucky rules, what five unwanted movements must be impossible before a cargo load counts as secure?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Loads count as secure only when nothing can slide, shift, fall, sift, or fly.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What gear secures cargo, why must loads and pets get rechecked, and whose view must high loads never block?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Cargo gets roped, netted, or tarped without overload, double-checked, pets included, against braking, bumps, and tailgaters' eyes.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: What are the limits of driver-assist tech on road checks and daily drives, and what three upkeep habits keep it working?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Assistance tech from blind-spot warnings to auto-braking alerts or steers but never drives, stays banned in part on tests, and wants clean sensors, fresh software, and constant driver focus.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: What single standard makes cargo truly secure, and what single standard makes driver-assist technology safe?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.memory_hook: Zero cargo shift, full driver focus
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Cargo counts as secure only when nothing moves, while assistance tech counts only when the driver stays engaged.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: How far ahead must you signal an intersection turn in Kentucky, and should you copy a lead car's blinker blindly?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Turns start with corner searches for controls, walkers, and cars plus a signal, hold the lane nearest your direction, sight through to the farthest path point, then finish with smooth speed, a cancelled signal, and a rear check, signaling one hundred feet ahead of intersection turns and never copying a leader's blinker unless you also turn.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which lane edges launch right and left turns, and what lane rule governs multi-lane turns?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Right turns hug the right-most lane edge without a left swing, left turns yield to oncoming traffic from the left-most edge, and multi-lane turns pick one lane and stay married to it until done.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: When is a driveway turnabout appropriate, and what clear sight distance must exist both ways first?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: A turnabout legally reverses direction through a street, alley, or driveway when circling the block is impractical, demanding five hundred feet of visibility each way before you signal right, stop, and check sides and rear.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: How do you steer and align your vehicle while backing into a driveway for a turnabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Back to the driveway's near edge, crank fully right while creeping back, center and straighten to a stop, and on a two-lane road hug right of the center line or your own side when unmarked.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Which four steps complete a driveway turnabout cleanly for Kentucky's road-skills exam?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Shift to drive, check both ways, and when clear signal left into the proper lane with matching speed, mastering this move for the skills test.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: From which lane edges do right turns versus left turns launch?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Right turns launch from the right-most lane edge, while left turns launch from the left-most edge after yielding to oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How does car placement during a driveway turnabout differ from stopping on a two-lane road?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Driveway turnabouts center the car in the drive, while two-lane turnabouts hold right of the center line or your own side.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: What five elements should you scan approaching any intersection, and whom can you assume will yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Slow at every intersection and hunt for devices, crossing traffic, walkers and cyclists, road conditions, and blind corners, trusting no one to obey or yield.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What head-check pattern follows a full stop, and what two checks precede rolling on a fresh green?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: After stopping, scan crossing traffic and bikes with a left-right-left sweep, and on a fresh green confirm a clear path plus a gap wide enough to cross, land in lane, and reach speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: How should you handle buildings, parked rows, or tall trucks blocking your side view at a corner?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Look both ways even when cross traffic faces red or stop signs, edge out slowly past buildings or parked rows, wait out lane-blocking views, and never nose into the next lane to peek.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: Why should you never pull out in front of an approaching car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Never count on shared space or extra room, and never trust an active turn signal, since its driver may pass you first or simply have forgotten it.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which direction do Kentucky roundabouts circulate, who yields at entry, and what must you do when exiting?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Roundabouts circle traffic counterclockwise around a raised island with entering cars yielding to circulating ones, so slow down, heed the warning sign, enter against the clock, then signal and take your exit.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: Which two bus types trigger mandatory stops when loading or unloading, and when may you move again?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Stop for any halted school or church bus loading or unloading on any roadway, since children surprise, and stay stopped until every person clears and the bus rolls.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What is the single roadway setup where oncoming traffic need not stop for a flashing school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: The bus stop binds both directions on every road except opposite-side travel on a four-or-more-lane road split by an elevated barrier or unpaved median, and no vehicle may pass a bus flashing its stop arm and lights.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: Why do both a brand-new green light and a cross street's red light still demand visual checks?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Fresh greens demand a patience check for crossing traffic, while reds and stops facing others still demand a both-way look.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Who must stop for a flashing school bus on two-lane or painted-median roads versus barrier-split four-lane highways?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Bus stops bind traffic in both directions, while the lone exception frees only opposite-side drivers on a divided four-or-more-lane road.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: Where does legal parking belong, and what three steps open a perpendicular stall entry?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Parked cars must never menace, so use marked areas, sit far from traffic flow or tight to the curb, respect signed, painted, and colored-curb bans, and begin perpendicular entries by spotting a space, checking traffic, and signaling.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How far straight back must you creep from a perpendicular space before turning the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Finish perpendicular entries by creeping centered to the space front and securing the car, and exit by backing straight until your front bumper clears the neighbor, then cranking toward the rear's path before driving off smooth and straight.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: When backing into a parallel curb space, what bumper-to-bumper landmark signals quick counter-steering?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Parallel entries start with space, traffic, and signal, then reverse while gazing rearward with quick wheel work until your front bumper lines with the lead car's rear bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: Once centered in a parallel spot, which side should you exit when safe, and what three lockup steps does law mandate?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Center into the slot, stop short of the rear bumper, drive-adjust, immobilize with brake and park or reverse gear, slip out curbside, and obey the law: engine off, key out, doors locked.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: When pulling out of a parallel space for your skills test, what cabin landmark must clear the lead car's rear bumper?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Parallel exits brake and back toward the rear car, then check, signal, and drive forward into the lane once the door post clears the lead car's rear bumper, re-reversing short of clearance, a maneuver to master for skills day.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: How do you angle parked wheels on hills with versus without curbs, even during a brief errand?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Aim hill-parked wheels to catch the curb if you roll, or off the road where curbless, then kill the engine, pocket the key, and lock up even for short stops.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Who may legally park in handicapped bays, and which Kentucky office issues disability plates or decals?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Handicapped bays serve only permitted vehicles carrying a disabled person, with violators fined and applicants directed to the County Clerk for decals or plates.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How does your front bumper's cue differ between backing out of a ninety-degree bay and backing into parallel?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Perpendicular exits back straight until the front bumper clears, while parallel entries reverse until the front bumper aligns.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: How do hill wheel angles combine with Kentucky's mandatory unattended-vehicle lockup steps?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Hill parking aims wheels at the curb or off the road, while every stop ends with engine off, key out, and doors locked.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: How are three-lane highways organized by speed and move—and what left-lane habit is illegal on limited-access highways?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Three-or-more lanes give middles to through traffic, the left to passers and left-turners, and the right to slower, entering, and right-turning drivers, while two-lane roads flow smoothest right with the left saved for passing, and camping the left lane of a limited-access highway breaks the law.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: Which lane must your turn finish in, and how should you handle missing a turn or entering a turn lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Turn into your nearest lane, with multi-lane lefts starting nearest center and rights nearest curb before any later change, loop around when you miss a turn, and follow through once committed in an intersection since last-second swerves collide.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Which two visual checks open every safe lane change before you move over?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Lane changes open with mirrors and an over-the-shoulder blind-spot check toward your move.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: After checking mirrors and blind spots, what four actions complete a smooth lane change?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Complete the change by spotting a gap, signaling, glancing again, and steering in at matched speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: How do you merge from an acceleration lane onto a freeway, and who holds right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Join freeways via the acceleration lane at traffic speed through a chosen gap with a cancelled signal, yielding to traffic already there.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: When exiting a freeway, where must you maintain normal speed and where should braking begin?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: Choose the lane nearest your exit well ahead of time and keep your current speed on the main roadway. Signal before moving into the deceleration lane, then slow down and check that lane’s posted speed.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: How does lane assignment shift between a three-plus-lane road and a two-lane same-way road?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: With at least three lanes in one direction, use the middle for through travel, the left for passing or a left turn, and the right for slower travel, entry or a right turn. With two lanes in one direction, reserve the left for passing.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What is the right play when you miss your turn versus once you commit to a turn lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Missed turns loop around at the next intersection, while committed turns follow through without last-second swerves.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: How do acceleration lanes and deceleration lanes handle highway speed transitions oppositely?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Highway entries speed up in the acceleration lane and yield to existing flow, while exits hold speed and then slow in the deceleration lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Which side handles normal passing, and under what rare condition may you leave pavement to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Pass on the left as a rule with the left-most lane reserved for it, pass right only when truly safe since right-side cars hide and surprise, and never leave the roadway unless the passed car fully stops and the move stays safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: How do broken-and-solid yellow centerlines govern passing, and within what oncoming footage must you finish?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: A solid line on your side of a broken line bans passing while a solid yellow left of a broken yellow permits it with no oncoming traffic and sign approval, and Kentucky law demands the pass finish before any no-passing zone and before closing within two hundred feet of oncoming cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: During a brisk left pass, what mirror sight tells you enough room exists to signal back right?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Pass briskly yet safely with oncoming, mirror, and shoulder checks plus a signal, glide over at adjusted speed, hold out until the passed car's full front fills your rearview, signal back, and merge smooth.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: Why must you never start a pass on blind hills or curves, or near crossroads, schools, and shops?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Weigh space at hills, curves, intersections, and obstacles, treat every blind hill or curve as hiding oncoming traffic and never start there, and shun passing near crossroads, crowds, shops, schools, parks, and crossings where blocked views and side entries ambush.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: How much lateral space do bicycles and scooters get when you pass—and may you cross a no-passing stripe?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Pull out only with room to return, declining multi-car gambles and borrowed space, and return once the passed car shows in your outside mirror; give same-direction bikes and scooters a full left-lane shift when lanes allow or three feet of left-side room on single lanes, cross the center even past no-passing paint when the left runs clear, and stay cautious when three feet will not fit.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: What does Kentucky law require of you when another vehicle pulls out to pass your car?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: When overtaken, hold your lane, and Kentucky law orders you to yield right to the passer while all road users cooperate for clearance.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Between a solid yellow stripe and a broken yellow stripe, how do you know whether your side may pass?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: A solid line on your side bans the pass, while a solid yellow left of the broken yellow permits it.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: How does your clearance rule when passing a car compare with passing a cyclist?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Car passes return once the passed car fills the outside mirror, while bike passes keep three feet of left-side room throughout.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What do right-of-way laws actually establish, and does any driver ever own right-of-way automatically?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Right-of-way rules set who yields first and the order for entering and crossing intersections, yet nobody ever owns the right of way automatically, so every approach demands a fresh read of the scene.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Who yields at a staggered stop, on a left turn, and when two cars reach a four-way stop together?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Yield to the driver who arrived first, to opposing traffic including right-turning vehicles when you turn left, and to the driver on your right when both of you reach a four-way stop at once.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Who yields when pulling from a driveway, minor street, or freeway ramp—and who wins inside an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Yield to highway traffic when pulling out of a driveway or private road, to main-road drivers when joining from a minor road, to freeway traffic already rolling when you enter from a ramp, and to any pedestrian, cyclist, or driver still inside the intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Across signals, signs, lane paint, crews, guards, and police officers, whose command overrides everything else?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Control devices span signals, signs, pavement markings, and live direction from officers, highway crews, and school guards, and an officer's orders overrule every sign and signal where two roads meet.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does arrival order decide four-way stops, and what breaks an exact tie?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: First arrival wins the intersection, while a simultaneous four-way stop gives the nod to the driver on your right.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: How are red, yellow, and green lenses arranged on vertical versus horizontal traffic signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Stacked signals read red over yellow over green from the top, while horizontal city signals read red left, yellow center, and green right, with lone single-color lights posted at some spots.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What must you yield to on a circular green light, especially before turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: A green light lets you go straight or turn after yielding to everyone lawfully in the intersection, and a left on green still waits for opposing through traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What does a steady yellow signal require, and where does Kentucky draw the line on red-light violations?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Yellow warns the signal is turning red, so stop when you safely can; clearing the box on red after a yellow entry is lawful, but entering after red is against the law.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Where must you halt on a steady red light, and when is turning right on red allowed?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: On red, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line until green, then turn right when the way is clear of cars and pedestrians unless a sign bans it.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Under what sole street-type pairing may you turn left on red, and into which lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Left on red is legal only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a full stop and a clear road, and any one-way turn lands in the nearest lane running your direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What different actions do a flashing yellow light and a flashing red light command?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: A flashing yellow orders slower speed and a sharp watch at crossings, work areas, and service trucks, while a flashing red demands a full stop before moving through clear space.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What must you do at twin flashing red railroad lights, and how do you treat a plain crossbuck?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Twin flashing reds guard a railroad crossing, so stop until the flashing ends and no train nears, and treat the nearby crossbuck exactly like a yield sign.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: How do steady green, flashing yellow, upward green, and steady red arrows direct your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.memory_hook: Green goes, yellow yields, red bans
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: A steady green arrow sends you that way from the proper lane, a flashing yellow arrow urges a careful proceed, an upward green arrow means straight ahead, and a red arrow bans that turn until green, always obeying the head above your lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How does a steady yellow traffic light differ in meaning from a flashing yellow beacon?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: A steady yellow means the light is turning red, while a flashing yellow only orders slower speed and a sharper watch.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: What separates a flashing yellow beacon's rule from a flashing red beacon's rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Flashing yellow asks for caution, while flashing red demands a full stop before proceeding through clear space.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: After a legal full stop, how is right-on-red broader than left-on-red?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Right on red follows any legal stop, while left on red works only from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: How does protection change when a steady green turn arrow switches to a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A steady green arrow grants the turn from the proper lane, while a flashing yellow arrow only permits a careful proceed.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: What does the round yellow railroad sign warn you to do ahead of the white crossbuck?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: The round yellow railroad warning sign means tracks are ahead: reduce speed, look and listen, and prepare to stop for a train. At the white crossbuck, an approaching train or rail vehicle requires stopping behind the line or before the crossing until it is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Why must you visually check every rail in both directions even if no track-count plaque or lights appear?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: A posted track count warns that several trains may cross, yet many multi-track crossings carry no such sign and some crossings lack lights entirely, so check every track in both directions yourself.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: How should you cross clear railroad tracks, and where must you wait if traffic backs up ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Cross rails briskly without stopping after looking both ways, wait while a train passes or until gates and lights release you, and when traffic forces a stop, halt at the line ahead of the rails.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: If your car stalls on railroad tracks, which direction do you run and whom do you call?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Stalled or boxed on the tracks, leave the car at once and run toward the oncoming train and away from the rails to dodge flying debris, then from a safe distance call the eight hundred number by the crossbuck or call nine one one, and never restart until a dispatcher says it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: How far can a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train roll before stopping, and why wait after one clears?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: A freight train at fifty-five miles per hour may need a mile or more to stop, so after one train passes on multi-track rails, wait for a clear view both ways, cross only with room to clear fully, and never stop on the crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: What mindset belongs at every railroad crossing, and what happens if you drive around lowered gates?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Expect a train at every crossing, because rolling past flashing warnings or lowered gates breaks the law and earns a citation.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How does the round yellow railroad board's role differ from the white crossbuck's stop rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A round yellow railroad sign gives advance warning of tracks; at the white crossbuck, stop behind the line or before the crossing when a train or rail vehicle approaches, and wait for a clear crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: What shape and colors mark standard warning boards, and where does fluorescent yellow-green appear?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Warning signs flag possible danger ahead in black on yellow diamonds, urging slower speed and stop readiness, with fluorescent yellow reserved for school zones, school crossings, and pedestrian crossings.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: What color marks construction and maintenance zones, and which temporary controls must you obey inside them?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Orange diamond or rectangular work-zone boards mark construction, maintenance, and emergency work with warnings of crews, slower speeds, detours, slow equipment, and shifting surfaces, so obey flaggers and signs, follow drums, cones, tubes, and temporary signals, and stop at any white line.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How do you protect highway crews in work zones, and what penalty hits work-zone speeders?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Give road workers a brake by slowing down, staying ready for sudden stops, refusing to tailgate, and remembering that work-zone speeding fines double.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What colors mark regulatory boards, what does a red circle-and-slash mean, and what condition caps speed limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Regulatory signs speak the law in white squares, rectangles, or special shapes with black, red, or green markings, covering direction, lanes, turns, speed, and parking, with a red ring and slash banning the pictured act, while black-and-white speed boards cap legal speed for ideal conditions.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: How do the eight-sided stop board and downward-pointing triangle yield board differ in shape and duty?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: An eight-sided red stop sign with white letters orders a stop behind the line or crosswalk plus a yield to crossing traffic and walkers in every direction, and a red-and-white downward triangle yield sign orders slowing until right-of-way traffic passes.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What are shared center turn lanes limited to, and what do wrong-way and do-not-enter boards guard?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: A shared center lane serves left turns from either side only and never through traffic or passing, one-way signs permit travel in the arrow's direction alone, wrong-way signs warn you are headed against traffic at ramps and one-way starts, and do-not-enter signs bar entry at those same spots.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What separates the physical requirement of an eight-sided red board from a red-and-white triangle?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: The eight-sided red stop sign orders a complete halt, while the downward red-and-white triangle only orders slowing for right-of-way traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: How do white boards, yellow diamonds, and green-brown-blue boards divide roadway messages?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: White regulatory boards state laws you must obey, while yellow diamonds warn of danger and green, brown, or blue guides inform and direct.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Which destinations do green, brown, and blue square or rectangular guide boards point toward?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Guide signs in green, brown, or blue squares and rectangles point to crossing roads, towns, sights, hospitals, fuel, food, and lodging.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: What do highway route shields identify, and how should you prepare before driving unfamiliar territory?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Route shields use shape and color to name interstate, federal, state, city, county, and local roads, so map your route first and then trail the shields through strange country.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Which five traffic-organization jobs do painted road lines, arrows, words, and symbols handle?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Painted lines, arrows, words, and symbols split lanes, govern passing and lane changes, assign turn lanes, outline walkways, and mark stop points for signs and signals.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: Where do you halt when a stop line precedes a crosswalk—and what if an intersection lacks painted lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Crosswalks frame legal pedestrian crossings, so halt behind the stop line, crosswalk, or sign and yield to anyone entering or inside, stay wary since many crossings lack paint, stop ahead of the intersection when no crossing shows, and honor a stop line before the crosswalk first.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: On standard traffic boards, what do red, green, and yellow backgrounds communicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.memory_hook: Red forbids, green guides, yellow warns
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Standard sign colors read red for stop or forbidden, green for permitted movement and guidance, and yellow for general warning.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: What messages belong to horizontal rectangles, triangles, vertical rectangles, diamonds, pentagons, and round boards?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.memory_hook: Guide, yield, law, hazard, school, rail
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Standard shapes read horizontal rectangle for guides, lone triangle for yield, vertical rectangle for regulation, diamond for present or possible hazards, pentagon for schools, and round for railroad and advance warning.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Which four distinct silhouettes announce yield, hazards, schools, and railroad crossings?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Triangles serve yield alone, diamonds mark present or possible hazards, pentagons mark schools, and round boards warn of railroads.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: How do red, green, and yellow divide prohibition, permission, and caution on road boards?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.memory_hook: Red stops, green permits, yellow warns
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Red stops or forbids, green permits movement and guides, and yellow warns in general.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which Kentucky license letters cover everyday cars, mopeds only, motorcycles, and commercial rigs?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.memory_hook: D car, E moped, M bike
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Class D is the basic operator license most drivers carry, Class E covers mopeds only, Class M covers motorcycles, and Classes A through C are commercial.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How do weight ratings, trailer limits, hazmat placards, and passenger seats divide CDL Classes A, B, and C?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.memory_hook: A heavy tow, B heavy, C
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: CDL A covers combined ratings of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more with tow ratings over ten thousand; B covers singles at twenty-six thousand one or more towing up to ten thousand; C covers lighter placarded hazmat or designs for over sixteen people, driver included.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Do volunteer church or school bus drivers need a CDL, and which five vehicle uses are exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: CDL rules reach volunteers such as church and school bus drivers, yet spare private cars, military and rescue rigs, campers, and farm trucks within one hundred fifty miles of home.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Who qualifies to apply for a Kentucky Class D license, which groups are exempt, and who is barred?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Class D wants fifteen-year-old residents with parents signing below eighteen plus three passed tests, while duty military, licensed dependents, working nonresidents, and farm rigs skip licensing and the under-fifteen, suspended, incompetent, unsafe, or English-illiterate are barred.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What four mechanical caps define a Kentucky moped, and how can a 16-year-old earn a Class E license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Mopeds capped at two horsepower, fifty cubic centimeters, automatic shifting, and thirty miles per hour need sixteen-year-old credentialed riders, or a Class E earned through knowledge and vision tests alone.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: What visibility and helmet guidance applies on a moped, and which highways are off-limits?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Use a headlight and space cushion on mopeds; helmets are optional but advised. Mopeds cannot use limited-access highways with minimum speeds over thirty miles per hour.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: What wheel and seating setup defines a motorcycle, where may unlicensed minibikes ride, and how does the permit path work?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Motorcycles seat riders astride at most three wheels with minibikes demanding full credentials on roads and private land alone excusing the unlicensed, while permits serve intermediate holders and adults at regional offices toward a held permit, a State Police road test, and a fee or a RideSmartKY certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What perk do rider-course graduates get, and in what exact step order do State Police applicants test?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Rider-course graduates skip motorcycle tests and may upgrade expired permits, while all applicants file at fifteen-plus with intact privileges before State Police vision, written, permit, and road-test sequencing that ends at the written for mopeds.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: Which three Kentucky license letters cover non-commercial driving, and which three cover commercial tiers?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.memory_hook: D E M civilian, A-B-C pro
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Class D, E, and M letters mark non-commercial driving while A, B, and C mark commercial weight and passenger tiers.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Which first-time Kentucky license class skips the behind-the-wheel skills exam completely?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: Moped riders earn Class E through knowledge and vision tests alone, while every other first-timer also faces a skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: What must a parent or legal guardian bring and sign at the site for an applicant under 18?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Under-eighteen applicants need a parent or guardian to accept joint liability by signing at the test site beside a birth certificate or court guardianship papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What three licensing phases do Kentucky teens progress through, and what power does a signing parent keep?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Teens climb three phases, permit then intermediate then full license, and a parent may withdraw responsibility anytime to cancel the credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which original documents must a teen permit seeker bring, how does residency proof change for REAL ID, and are copies allowed?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Permit seekers show a birth certificate, Social Security card, residency proof doubled for REAL ID, a school compliance form, and a signed parent, with photocopies refused.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: What hold period, practice hours, supervisor rule, passenger cap, and night curfew govern under-21 Kentucky permit holders?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Ages fifteen–twenty hold permits one hundred eighty days; intermediate eligibility needs sixty practice hours, ten at night. Carry the permit beside a licensed front-seat adult twenty-one-plus; at most one unrelated passenger under twenty. Under-eighteen midnight-to-six driving needs good cause.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What alcohol cutoff, 180-day clock penalty, and minor point threshold apply to under-21 permit holders?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Drivers under twenty-one meet zero alcohol tolerance at point zero two, see any moving or permit violation restart the one hundred eighty-day clock, and risk suspension past six points as minors.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: When may a teen book the State Police road check, what must they bring, may they drive there solo, and how long is a retry wait?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: After one hundred eighty days and turning seventeen, teens book a State Police road test with an insured registered vehicle, a signed sixty-hour log, and a week-fresh eligibility letter, never driving themselves there, with failure costing a week.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: What credential do you earn on passing the teen road check, what unlocks full licensing, and what excuses midnight-to-6 driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Passing earns an intermediate sticker; full licensing needs one hundred eighty days, driver education and age seventeen. Midnight-to-six driving needs good cause: emergency, school or work.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which four safety limits continue to apply to intermediate license holders under 18?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Intermediates under eighteen keep the one-young-passenger cap, zero tolerance, violation restarts, and the six-point suspension tripwire.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Where do teens upgrade to a full license, by what age must driver training finish, and what four course paths count?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Full licensure follows the course, one hundred eighty days, and age seventeen at a regional office with a paper temporary, and training must finish by nineteen through free classroom, twelve dollars and fifty cents online, high school, or a private four-hour course.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: In what two ways do completed driver-education courses get reported to Kentucky licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Some course completions self-report within two business days, while the rest travel by mail to Frankfort carrying license number, name, and birth date.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: What milestone does the first 180-day hold unlock, and what milestone does the second 180-day hold unlock?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The permit-side one hundred eighty days unlock the road test, while the intermediate-side one hundred eighty days unlock the full license.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What document rules, permit term, hold duration, and passenger requirement apply to new applicants aged 18 to 20?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: Drivers eighteen to twenty book State Police written and vision tests with four document types in original, then hold a three-year paper permit one hundred eighty days beside a twenty-one-or-older companion before the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: How long must a new driver aged 21 or older hold a permit before road testing, and what car and retry rules apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Road tests want insured registered cars with adult escorts and punish misses with a week, while drivers twenty-one-plus repeat the same papers and tests with only a thirty-day hold.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What first-time vision score passes directly, what floor applies after a specialist referral, and what does the written check cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: First-timers need twenty over forty vision with required lenses as a restriction and a twenty over sixty floor after specialist referral, then face a license-matched written test on rules, procedures, and signs from this manual.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What minimum percentage passes the Kentucky operator written exam, and in what formats is it available?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Operators must score at least eighty percent to pass the written test, which also runs orally, on tablets, and across many languages.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What paperwork and equipment does a State Police examiner inspect first, and what cabin rules govern the ride?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Examiners inspect registration, insurance, lights, signals, horn, wipers, and brakes, then ride the clean front passenger seat belted through normal traffic with no tricks and no in-car interpreter.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What visibility distances must high beams, low beams, and red taillights meet on a road-test car, and what cancels the check?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.memory_hook: Three-fifty high, one-hundred low, five-hundred rear
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Test cars need three hundred fifty-foot high beams, one hundred-foot lows, a five hundred-foot red taillight, working lamps, a lit legible plate, clear glass with a wiper, horn, muffler, mirrors, and steering, with missing or illegal gear canceling the test.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Which maneuvers get graded on the road check, what triggers an instant fail, and how many ignored instructions disqualify you?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: The road test grades stops, backing, turnarounds, hills, parking, intersections, clutch, speed, turns, lanes, right-of-way, and control, fails instantly on crashes or violations, drops drivers after two ignored instructions, reports only pass or fail, and enforces a week before retry.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: When and how do State Police testing appointments open, and what must applicants needing accommodations do first?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: All State Police testing runs appointment-only online with slots opening weekdays at eight a.m. roughly three weeks out, and anyone needing interpreters or aid must phone the site first.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does passing the Kentucky written exam differ from passing the road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The written test passes at eighty percent on rules questions, while the road test is judged live by a riding examiner.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: On the road skills check, how does the strike limit for a dangerous act compare with ignoring examiner instructions?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A single crash, violation, or dangerous act fails the road test at once, while ignored examiner instructions take two strikes to disqualify.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: How soon must new Kentucky residents transfer a license, when must they retest, and how are out-of-state permits handled?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: New residents must license within thirty days, testing only when long expired or lost behind a certified record, and file residency, presence, Social Security, and old-license papers while out-of-state permit holders swap permits first at fifteen-plus.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What licensing rules cover out-of-state college students, non-citizens with foreign licenses, and permanent residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: College students keep valid home licenses beside a Kentucky school ID, non-citizens drive a year on foreign licenses with international permits under reciprocity, and permanent residents test from written-only to all three exams by permit origin.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: What determines how many exams international-permit holders take, and what waives exams for both resident classes?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: International-permit holders face anywhere from written-only to all three exams by residency and reciprocity, valid United States licenses excuse both resident classes, and the permit-less restart with a Kentucky permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: How can stationed military members renew a Kentucky Class D license away from home or reclaim an expired one after returning?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: Stationed troops may renew Class D licenses by mail, reclaim expired ones test-free within ninety days of return, and otherwise follow standard expired-license steps.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: When do under-21 and adult licenses expire, how early can you renew, and what lapse triggers full retesting?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: Under-twenty-one licenses die ninety days after twenty-one while adult cards run thirty-one days past each birthday with six-month-early renewal, test-free below five years expired, four- or eight-year terms, and mail or office replacement.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: How quickly must you get a duplicate card after moving or changing your name, and how is a Social Security card treated?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Address or name changes demand a duplicate license within ten days under citation threat, with one legal proof for names and an updated Social Security card displayed but never accepted as that proof.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: How does Kentucky's 30-day license transfer deadline treat permanent new residents differently from college students?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: New residents must license within thirty days, while college students may keep a valid home license beside a school ID.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How do exam rules for civilians holding international permits compare with troops returning from duty?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Civilians with international permits test along a reciprocity ladder, while stationed troops renew test-free inside ninety days of return.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does the adult birthday renewal window compare with the deadline to update a changed name or address?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Birthdays allow thirty-one days to renew an adult license, while address or name changes allow only ten days for a duplicate.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: Which serious offenses strip a license, how can parents or drivers end one voluntarily, and when do unpaid crash judgments suspend?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.memory_hook: Grave crimes, parent cancel, sixty-day debt
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: Licenses fall to perjury, unlicensed driving, missing insurance, ignored courts, unpaid support, triple reckless years, DUI, test refusal, fleeing, hit-and-run, thefts, and vehicular manslaughter, while parents may cancel minors, drivers may surrender by form, and unpaid crash judgments suspend from sixty days.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: At how many points inside two years do adults and under-18 drivers face suspension, and what does skipping the hearing cost?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: Drivers start point-free, risk suspension at twelve points or seven below eighteen inside two years after a hearing, lose points after two years with five-year records, and skipping the hearing draws six months, then a year, then two.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: How often can a point hearing swap suspension for probation, and how often may court-referred drivers attend state traffic school?
