sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Hearings may trade suspension for probation plus traffic school, unrepeatable within two years, and the school takes court-referred licensed drivers with minor violations at most yearly as a court order whose breach suspends.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What mandatory assessment, program, fees, and wait stand between every DUI conviction and getting a license back?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: Every DUI conviction demands a human-resources-cabinet assessment plus an approved program with fees paid before reinstatement, and reissue further needs the fee, the completion notice, and a served suspension.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How do grave traffic crimes differ from routine moving violations in triggering a Kentucky suspension?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Single grave acts suspend driving at once, while lesser offenses suspend only at twelve points or seven below eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does eligibility for state traffic school differ from Kentucky's mandatory DUI education program?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Traffic school follows a court referral for minor violations, while a DUI program follows every conviction before any reinstatement.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Why does driving at night carry greater difficulty and danger than driving in daylight?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Night driving outranks daylight in difficulty and danger, with sight chained to headlight throw.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: When do high beams help or hurt, and at what exact distances must you dim them?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Burn high beams whenever none approach since they double low-beam reach, dip for oncoming metal, drop to lows behind followers and in fog, rain, or snow where highs glare, optionally fog-lamping storms, and always dim within five hundred feet of oncoming cars and three hundred feet of leaders.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Where should you look against oncoming glare, and how much extra following time does night require?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Glare-blind, aim eyes at the right edge while scanning past your beams for dark lumps, edge-check both shoulders, ditch sunglasses and tints at night and under clouds, pad following by at least one extra second at night and two on strange night roads, and switch lamps on whenever others look dim.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How far do high beams reach compared to lows, and when must you switch to low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: High beams reach twice as far as low beams and serve night travel without oncoming traffic. Use low beams while following or in fog, rain or snow; dim within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle and three hundred feet of a vehicle ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How do your eye aim in glare and your following gap on familiar versus strange night roads work?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Glare sends eyes to the right edge, while darkness pads gaps one second, two on strange roads.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What intersection rights does an escorted funeral procession hold, and who still outranks it?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Funeral columns own intersections behind yellow, red, or blue escort flashers, yielding only to emergency iron, police orders, and trains, so never split the column, fake right-of-way with lamps or stunts, or pass riders without orders or beyond city, town, and urban-county limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Which multi-lane highways allow passing a funeral procession, and what penalties hit violators?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Interstates and parkways also free procession passing, while violators face a two hundred fifty dollars fine or ninety days in jail.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Why must you slow inside every work zone, and what triggers doubled fines in Kentucky?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Work zones fence roadwork with closures, detours, and machines, wounding some forty thousand people yearly, so approach hunting orange-on-black signs, cones, barrels, trucks, and crews, always slowing for tight lanes and rough skin even when deserted, since Kentucky doubles signed-zone fines wherever at least one true worker stands.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: How should you drive through an active work zone until passing the End Road Work sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Inside zones, slow down, stretch gaps, track neighbors, coil to stop, drive doubly wary after dark, slide over for crews and iron, obey every board through End Road Work, budget delays with early starts, and detour around whenever possible.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Which three authorities or hazards still require an escorted funeral column to yield?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Escorted columns own intersections, excepting emergency iron, police orders, and trains.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Under which three exceptions may you overtake a funeral procession, and what penalty guards the rule?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: You may pass or overtake a funeral-procession vehicle only when directed by a police or safety officer, on a road outside city, town or urban-county limits, or on an interstate or state parkway. A violation of the procession law may result in a two hundred fifty dollars fine or ninety days in jail.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How does your speed duty in an empty work zone compare with Kentucky's doubled-fine trigger?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Every zone demands slowing, while doubled fines need signs plus one true worker.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: How must you adjust speed and lane position on loose gravel versus narrow ditch-lined rural strips?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Rural blacktop kills the unwary, so heed signs and limits; gravel and dirt sap grip, demanding slower speeds, longer gaps, and skid-ready stops, while narrow ditch-lined strips want centered slow cars watching for lane-borrowing opposites.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Who holds the right-of-way when two vehicles approach a narrow or single-lane rural bridge?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Heed narrow and single-lane bridge warnings and trade crossings, with first arrival holding the right-of-way.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: How should you handle open-grate bridge decks, blind wooded curves, and unmarked rural intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Steel and open-grate decks skate, so slow, gap, and grip hard; wooded, cropped, and hilly blind corners demand slow stop-ready rolling; and uncontrolled rural crossings want the same for crossing and oncoming metal.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What seating, controls, belts, and wheel count define an autocycle under Kentucky rules?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Autocycles seat riders car-style over three grounded wheels past forty miles per hour, side-by-side or tandem under open or capped tops, belted three-point with optional bags or cages, steered by wheel and pedals, yet never alternative-speed motorcycles.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Which traffic rules apply to autocycles, and do drivers need a motorcycle endorsement or helmet?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Autocycles count as motorcycles for traffic law but need no cycle license or endorsement beyond a valid operator's license, and riders skip headgear mandates.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: What specific danger does loose gravel pose compared with narrow ditch-lined country roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Gravel saps grip for stops, while narrow ditch strips threaten lane shares.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How do opposing drivers settle priority at a single-lane bridge?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Single-lane bridges trade crossings, with first arrival holding priority.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: What distinct hazards come from steel bridge grates, wooded hills, and uncontrolled rural crossroads?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.memory_hook: Grates skate, hills hide, crossroads surprise
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Steel decks skate under tires, blind corners hide behind woods and hills, and uncontrolled crossings surprise.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: How do Kentucky traffic duties and licensing-or-helmet rules split for autocycle operators?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Autocycles obey motorcycle law, yet skip cycle licenses and helmets.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What causes most trailer crashes, and how should cargo weight split front-to-back?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Towing spans billions of yearly miles with judgment as the linchpin, since driver error mothers most rig crashes, so hitch, load, and run correctly with sixty percent of cargo weight forward and forty percent aft to strangle sway.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: How do you calm a swaying trailer right away, and how do you fix the root cause?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Swaying, steer dead straight and bleed speed without brakes and never faster, park fully clear soonest, re-pin front-heavy loading with heavies floored, tight packing, and tied partials.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Near what top speed should towed rigs cruise, and when do you brake for hills?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Tow with a compensating mind at a lazier pace, capping near fifty-five miles per hour, never topping posted limits, slowing further as weather sours, and braking before grades begin.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: How do stopping distances, passing gaps, and cornering paths change when pulling a trailer?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Rigs stop and pass longer, so bank extra nose room swelling in rain, snow, and fog, budget hill and curve passes, and swing turns wide since trailers cheat inside.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Where does your steering hand go to aim a backing trailer, and how do you fix jackknifing?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Back trailers slowly with a bottom-wheel hand steering the tail where the hand points, and at jackknife freeze, pull ahead straight, then retry.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What pre-trip and fuel-stop habits keep long trailer hauls from ending in roadside breakdowns?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Pros counsel expert help when unsure, combination thinking, walk-around hitch, chain, light, and tire checks before rolling and at every fuel stop, safe pull-offs for strange noises, and rested daylight legs over straight-through marathons.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Which core mechanical, loading, and driver checks belong on every safe-towing checklist?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: The safe-tow checklist chants heavy front, tight hitch, chained, lit, aired, slowed, thinking ahead, rested, inspected, secured, and belted.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Which two pedal inputs must you strictly avoid while calming a swaying trailer?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Sway steers straight and bleeds speed, never braking nor speeding.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: What cruising speed ceiling and hill-braking habit fit safe trailer towing?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Rigs cap near fifty-five and brake before grades, banking longer stops and passes.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: What steering adjustments handle inside-cutting trailers on forward turns versus backing maneuvers?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: Turns swing wide for cheating trailers, while backing steers tails by bottom-hand.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: What equipment gets checked on walk-arounds, and how should long towing trips be paced?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: Walk-arounds recheck hitch, chains, lights, and tires, while long hauls rest and inspect often.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Which three crash-avoidance actions serve as every driver's escape tools during a road emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Emergencies find every driver, so preparation and crash prevention are universal duties with three escape tools: braking, steering, and accelerating.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: How should you brake during a sudden emergency in a car equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Stopping is the first crash-avoidance instinct, and most new cars carry anti-lock brakes that halt without skidding while preserving steering, so learn your owner's manual, then stomp and hold through normal vibration and clicks while still steering.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which emergency braking method should you follow if your vehicle lacks anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Cars without anti-lock brakes follow the owner's manual braking procedure instead.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What steering sequence lets you swerve around road trouble and safely regain straight control?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Swerving around trouble starts with a two-hand grip, aims where you want to go while dodging traffic, then counter-steers straight to regain control and slow down.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Where should your hands stay while driving, and how do you dodge obstacles or darting animals?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Keep both hands on the wheel except for brief driving tasks, and pair braking with steering against roadway obstacles, braking and steering to miss animals that dart out.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Under what kind of crash threat does speeding up become the safest escape choice?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Sometimes the escape is speed, as when another vehicle threatens from behind or the side.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How does emergency braking in an anti-lock car compare with braking in a non-anti-lock car?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Anti-lock cars stomp and hold through clicks and shudders, while non-anti-lock cars follow the owner's manual instead.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does a pure emergency swerve differ from dodging an animal that darts onto the road?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Swerves steer around and counter-steer straight, while animal encounters brake and steer together.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Which escape tools handle threats ahead versus threats closing in from behind or the side?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Braking and steering dodge threats ahead, while accelerating dodges strikes from behind or the side.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What three mistakes trigger a skid, and which driver reactions make a slide turn deadly?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Skids strike from excess speed, panic stops, or lost grip and leave little control, while panicking, brake-stomping, and overcorrecting only deepen the skid toward a fatal crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What is your first move in a skid, and how do you slow a straight slide with anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Skidding, release both pedals and stare where you want to go, adding steady brake pressure to slow a straight-line slide in an anti-lock car.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How should you slow down during a skid if your vehicle has no anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Without anti-lock brakes, never brake hard since locked wheels worsen skids; slow the car with gentle brake pumps instead.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: How do you steer out of a sideways rear-wheel skid without whipping into a second slide?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: In a sideways skid, steer toward the sliding rear to realign the nose, then unwind promptly as the car straightens to block a counter-skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: How long must you keep working the wheel in a skid, and which control matters most?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Keep seesawing the wheel until the skid fully releases, since the steering wheel outranks every other skid control.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: How do you safely return to the road after your tires drop off the pavement edge?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Off the pavement edge, refuse panic yanks back up; slow gradually and, when safe, turn briskly back on.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does braking inside a skid differ between anti-lock vehicles and plain-brake vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Anti-lock skids take steady brake pressure, while plain skids take gentle pumps and never a stomp.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: What two-step steering rhythm pulls a car cleanly out of a sideways skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Sideways skids steer into the sliding rear, then unwind fast to block the counter-skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What must you do immediately after any crash in Kentucky, and where do non-injury wrecks go?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: After any collision, stop at or near the scene, stay until the officer finishes questioning, and under Kentucky law shift non-injury wrecks to the shoulder per KRS one hundred eighty-nine point five eight zero, subsection one, paragraph b.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: Which driver, vehicle, insurance, and scene details should you record after a collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Log every operator's name, address, and license number, each car's plate, VIN, make, model, and year, each insurer's name and phone, a damage list with photos, and exactly what happened just before and after impact.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What are your legal duties if you bump an unattended parked car and cannot find the owner?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: For parked-car strikes, hunt the owner or leave a visible note bearing your name, address, license and plate numbers, plus the date and time.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: When must you file a civilian crash report with Kentucky State Police, and what is the deadline?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Property damage over five hundred dollars without a police investigation demands a written report to the Kentucky State Police within ten days of the crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: How should you care for injured crash victims, and when is moving someone permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Aid the injured with prompt proper care, summon medics and troopers with a precise location, move victims only to save a life, otherwise await the ambulance while blanketing them warm.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: What reasonable aid duties does Kentucky law place on every driver involved in a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Kentucky law orders every involved operator to stop at once, size up injuries and damage, and render reasonable aid including carrying or arranging transport for treatment when plainly needed or requested.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How does handling an injury crash scene differ from handling a non-injury crash in Kentucky?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Injury scenes hold position until questioned, while non-injury wrecks shift to the shoulder.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: How does information exchange in a two-driver crash differ from hitting an empty parked car?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Driver-to-driver crashes log full identities and damage, while parked-car strikes leave a dated note.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: Which two ways can a civilian collision report be submitted, and when do you skip filing?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Collision reports e-file through the portal or mail to Frankfort, but never when an officer investigated.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Under what sole condition may crash victims be moved instead of waiting blanketed for medics?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Victims move only to save a life, otherwise awaiting the ambulance under blankets.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: How do you prevent mechanical breakdowns, and which dashboard warning lamp demands stopping right away?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Honor the owner's manual service schedule to head off failures, watch warning lamps, and never drive under a brake warning.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: How should you apply the parking brake if your main foot brakes fail while rolling?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Brakeless while rolling, drag the parking brake slowly against rear-wheel lockup and skid, poised to release if the tail steps out.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What last-resort steps stop your vehicle if both main brakes and parking brake fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: If the parking brake fails too, kill the engine, coast to a safe off-road stop, and never drive on without working brakes.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: How does steering pull differ between a front-tire blowout and a rear-tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Blowouts vent tires instantly, yanking front-tire cars hard toward the burst side while rear-tire cars wobble, shake, and drift that way.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: What should your hands and feet do the instant a tire blows out at speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: On a blowout, clamp the wheel straight, lift off the gas, and shun the brake, letting the car coast down or braking only feather-light.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Where should you stop to change a blown tire, and what warning lights go on?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Never halt on the roadway when avoidable; limp to a safe shoulder, flash the hazards, and fit a fresh tire.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: How do you steer and brake to safety when your engine stalls while moving?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Dead engine rolling, muscle the heavy-but-turnable wheel, pick an escape path, and brake steadily rather than hard while easing off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Once a stalled vehicle stops off the road, what steps do you take if restarting fails?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Halted, retry the starter, and on failure raise the hood, light the flashers, and call for help.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What sequence safely stops your car if the accelerator sticks down while driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: For a runaway accelerator, switch the engine off, grab neutral, find an escape path, steer smooth, brake soft, pull clear, and fix the pedal before driving again.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: Where should you park a disabled vehicle, and which two blind road spots are forbidden?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Breakdowns kill visibility, so park fully off to the right when possible or where distant drivers can spot you, never just past a crest or bend, flashing hazards with the hood raised.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: How far behind a broken-down car do warning flares belong, and whom should you phone?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Plant warning flares two hundred to three hundred feet behind the disabled car to buy lane-change time, and phone authorities, whose numbers many roadways post.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: In what exact order do you use backup stopping methods when your main brakes fail?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Dead brakes try the parking brake first, then the engine switch as the last resort.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: How can you tell a front-tire blowout apart from a rear-tire blowout by feel?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Front blowouts yank toward the burst side, while rear blowouts wobble, shake, and drift.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: How does your first move for a dead engine differ from a stuck runaway accelerator?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Power failures brake steadily to the shoulder, while runaway accelerators switch off and grab neutral first.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Which road features must disabled cars avoid, and how far back should flares sit?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Breakdowns shun crests and bends for parking, then plant flares two hundred to three hundred feet behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Which five checks and steps make up starting your vehicle in Kentucky?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Checking fuel, anti-lock brake, and airbag warning lights before moving catches critical system faults early.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: How should your shifter, eyes, blinker, and right heel work together when pulling away from a stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Resting your heel on the floorboard lets your ankle modulate smooth throttle instead of jerking forward.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What three-step habit brings your car to a smooth, safe everyday stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Glancing in the mirror before lifting off the gas reveals tailgaters so you can brake gradually.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Whether moving forward or backing in reverse, which direction do you turn the steering wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: New drivers often second-guess reverse steering—wanting the tail right still means turning the wheel right.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Where does the vehicle-starting chain finish compared with the moving-off chain?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Keeping startup separate from pull-away prevents rushing into drive before warning lights finish cycling.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How do foot braking and steering direction pair up across normal stops and maneuvers?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Smooth right-foot transitions keep weight balanced while consistent directional steering avoids parking-lot mistakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Why did driver training retire the old ten-and-two steering-wheel hand placement?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: High hands sitting across the upper rim get blasted into your face if the steering-hub airbag inflates.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Where and how should your fingers, thumbs, and palms hold the steering wheel today?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Hooking inside spokes or palming the rim can sprain wrists violently if a pothole jerks the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Which clock-face hand position is retired for airbag safety, and which outside grip replaces it?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Dropping hands down to nine and three clears the airbag blast path while boosting steering leverage.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What outside check should open every backing maneuver, and why isn't sitting in the driver's seat enough?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and toys sit completely below rear trunk glass where cabin sightlines never reach.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: How should your foot, both hands, and eyes be positioned when backing straight?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Draping your right arm across the passenger headrest pivots your shoulders cleanly toward the rear window.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Why can't you rely solely on mirrors while backing up?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Side and interior glass leave a wide blind wedge directly behind the trunk lid.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: How fast should you roll in reverse, and how big should steering inputs be?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Rear-end steering pivots sharply—tiny wheel nudges at creeping speed prevent wild tail swings.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What extra glances do turning reverses require, and how long must your main gaze stay rearward?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Swinging your front bumper wide demands brief side checks, yet turning forward before halting invites bumper hits.
sec05-card-sec05-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Quick front-side checks; rear-gaze until stopped

visual_sync.text_span: Quick front-side checks; rear-gaze until stopped

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How does a pre-backing walk-around complement what your mirrors can see?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Combining an outside lap with mirror scans closes both low close-in and distant aisle hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does your stationary reverse setup pair with your moving reverse technique?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Setting twelve-o'clock hand and rear-window gaze first makes slow steering corrections effortless once rolling.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Why must safe drivers keep their eyes moving in every direction instead of staring at one spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Target fixation freezes awareness—active scanning buys precious seconds to adjust speed or lane position smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How far ahead should your forward scan reach, and why shouldn't you tuck close behind tall trucks?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Tailgating a tall trailer shrinks a thirty-second horizon down to a blind wall of metal.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Before which four everyday maneuvers must you sweep your mirrors to check traffic behind?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Knowing whether a heavy pickup sits two lengths off your bumper dictates how gently you brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Along with matching road conditions and keeping a safe gap, how often should you check your speedometer?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Smooth highway asphalt masks velocity creep—a quick once-a-minute speedometer glance catches accidental speeding.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What are Kentucky's four unposted default speeds across interstates, state highways, business-residential streets, and public parking lots?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Memorize that descending ladder—select interstates only reach seventy when officially posted by the secretary.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What caps nighttime speed, and what legal maximum applies when fog, snow, or rain cuts visibility to one hundred feet?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: High beams bounce blinding glare off thick fog—drop to low beams and cap speed at twenty-five.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: How should you approach overgrown corners and enter blind hills or curves?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Entering every blind crest slow enough to halt protects you if a tractor sits stalled beyond.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How do your twenty-to-thirty-second forward gaze and your side-and-mirror sweeps divide scanning jobs?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Forward sight previews traffic slowdowns while side and mirror glances catch crossers and tailgaters.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How do Kentucky's unposted highway limits step down once you enter town districts and public lots?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Pedestrian density climbs sharply from rural blacktop to storefronts and parking aisles, cutting legal speed.
sec08-card-sec08-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Sixty-five-fifty-five open; thirty-five town; fifteen lot

visual_sync.text_span: Sixty-five-fifty-five open; thirty-five town; fifteen lot

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Compare the speed rule for clear nighttime driving with heavy weather under one hundred feet of sight?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Both rules tie speed directly to clear stopping sight rather than dry daytime sign numbers.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: When should you finish braking for a curve, and why avoid hard mid-curve braking?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Hard braking while tires are already loaded sideways snaps cornering grip and triggers a skid.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: On wet or icy roads, how does braking technique differ without anti-lock brakes versus with them?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Pumping an anti-lock pedal defeats its computer pulsing—hold steady pressure so steering stays alive.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What happens during hydroplaning, and how should you treat deep standing water across a roadway?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Pooled water lifts rubber completely off asphalt—keep firm tread, slow down, and turn around at floods.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What span does total stopping distance cover, and how long does alert perception time average?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Even an alert brain spends nearly a full second recognizing danger before your right foot moves.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How long does foot-reaction time average, and roughly how far is pure braking distance from fifty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Adding perception and reaction travel onto one hundred fifty-eight braking feet shows why tailgaters crash.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Where does speed scrubbing belong on a winding road so tires hold cornering traction?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Entering slow lets gentle throttle settle weight evenly through the apex without sliding wide.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: How do your right-foot motions reverse between standard brakes and anti-lock brakes on slick pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Knowing which brake system your vehicle carries keeps panic stops straight on icy mornings.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How does smart driving on ordinary wet asphalt differ from meeting deep pooled water?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Good tread channels ordinary rain at reduced speed, whereas deep water hides washouts and stalls engines.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: How does perception time fit inside total stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Every distracted glance stretches perception time, adding invisible yards before your foot ever leaves the gas.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: How do reaction time and fifty-mile-per-hour dry braking distance split the physical stop?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: At fifty miles per hour, two seconds of perception-and-reaction plus braking pass two hundred fifty feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: What safety asset does keeping an open space cushion on all four sides buy you?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Surrounding your car with open asphalt gives you somewhere to brake or steer when neighbors err.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Which collision type leads crash statistics, and what minimum following gap does Kentucky's manual set?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Note Kentucky's stricter four-second baseline—riding bumpers blinds forward sight and violates tailgating law.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: How do you measure Kentucky's minimum following cushion using a roadside landmark?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: If your front bumper passes that shadow or sign before one-thousand-four finishes, ease off and recount.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Under which five road, weather, or lead-vehicle situations must you stretch past four seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop and swerve rapidly while hazmat tankers and buses halt abruptly at rail crossings.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: How should you help when a trailing vehicle pulls out to overtake and merge ahead of you?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Lifting off the gas opens a clean pocket ahead so the passer clears opposing lanes fast.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: How should you manage side cushions, other drivers' blind spots, and oncoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Lingering beside someone's rear quarter panel invites a lane-change sideswipe—move ahead or drop back.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: How do you pad freeway mergers, walkers, wide trucks, parked doors, and interstate shoulder parkers?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Moving into the left interstate lane early protects stranded motorists and troopers working along shoulders.
sec08-card-sec08-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Make room; shift left past shoulders

visual_sync.text_span: Make room; shift left past shoulders

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Which three smooth habits protect your rear bumper when someone tailgates behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Extra space ahead lets you decelerate gradually for both cars instead of braking hard.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: Which four defensive responses let you absorb another driver's mistake before metal meets?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Giving up right-of-way with a calm brake tap or lane shift beats winning an argument inside a tow truck.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How does Kentucky's dry-daylight following count compare with bad-weather or special-vehicle following?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Four seconds handles ideal dry pavement—storms, darkness, big rigs, and motorcycles all demand extra seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Compare how you clear a neighbor's blind spot versus how you defuse a tailgater on your bumper?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Brisk pace adjustments clear side pockets, whereas smooth predictable braking protects your own rear bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What risky reverse move should you avoid into live streets, and who can assist tight backing?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: A trusted spotter standing safely off to the side sees low obstacles hidden behind your trunk.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What is the only legal move after rolling past your intended interstate exit?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Backing down an interstate shoulder or ramp puts you head-on against seventy-mile-per-hour freeway traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: What two goals define effective driver communication on the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Making your vehicle easy to spot while signaling moves early eliminates surprises for everyone nearby.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: Between what sunset-to-sunrise clock times—and during what visibility moments—must Kentucky headlamps shine?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Plus rain, snow, fog, dusk, sun glare, or anytime cars look dim—if they look dim, so do you.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: When is a light horn tap helpful, and near whom is honking strictly forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Angry blasts startle motorists and scramble acoustic bearings for visually impaired pedestrians using canes or dogs.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: Beyond corner turns and lane changes, which other lateral moves and slowdowns require signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Pulling away from a curb or nosing onto a shoulder shifts lateral space and needs a blinker.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Must you signal on empty roads, do signals grant right-of-way, and are arm hand-signals legal in Kentucky?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Catch that Kentucky-specific test rule—hand signals are prohibited, so working electric turn lamps are mandatory.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Why should your turn blinker come on before your foot touches the brake for a mid-block driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Blinking before slowing explains why you are braking where no traffic light or turn bay exists.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: How does acceptable backing help in a tight lot contrast with missing a highway exit?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Slow reversing with a spotter belongs in driveways, never on high-speed interstate ramps or shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Where does Kentucky draw the line between helpful horn communication and prohibited honking?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Keep horn use strictly polite and protective—never vent frustration or startle blind pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: Summarize Kentucky's four rules on when signals run, what they grant, what type is legal, and afterward?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Flashing an electric lamp announces your plan—you still wait for a safe gap and cancel afterward.
sec08-card-sec08-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Before moves, zero priority, mechanical, cancel

visual_sync.text_span: Before moves, zero priority, mechanical, cancel

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How must drivers yield and adjust speed around crosswalks, intersections, neighborhoods, and flashing school zones?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Green lights and unmarked corners never erase your duty to yield when pedestrians occupy the street.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Where must you stop for a blind pedestrian with a cane or guide dog, and what fine applies?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Stopping within five feet lets blind walkers hear your engine idle unless you drive silent electric.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Which actions must you avoid around a blind pedestrian, and what cue says you may proceed?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Shouting directions or honking drowns out the traffic audio cues blind travellers trust to stay alive.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does your duty toward pedestrians anywhere compare with walkers in crosswalks and intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Scanning every curb prevents surprises while giving immediate right-of-way inside marked or unmarked crosswalks.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How does Kentucky's penalty for failing to yield to white-cane or guide-dog walkers stand apart?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Ignoring a white cane or assistance dog risks a pedestrian's life and brings two hundred fifty dollars.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: How should you behave while a blind walker decides, and what gesture clears you to drive?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Stepping back and folding the cane is the unmistakable sign that the walker declined crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How does Kentucky traffic law classify bicycles, and what mistakes do novice riders often make?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Narrow bike frames vanish in glare while inexperienced riders wobble unexpectedly or roll past stop signs.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Where must drivers yield to cyclists, and under what five exceptions may cars enter bike lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Treating painted bike lanes like extra turn pockets clips riders who legally hold straight-through priority.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: How should motorists handle speed, turns, horns, and slick surfaces when driving near cyclists?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Turning right directly across a cyclist's nose or braking hard ahead overwhelms skinny bicycle tires.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: How and over what minimum distance must non-motor vehicles signal before making a turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Brief intermittent hand or lamp signals let cyclists return both hands to handlebars before cornering.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Why might a cyclist skip hand signals, and when must parked drivers scan for bikes?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Flinging a parked car door open without checking mirrors launches passing cyclists straight into traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: How much minimum side clearance and merge space must you give when passing a bicycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Cutting back right too early clips the front wheel or buffets the rider off balance.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Which five narrow situations allow a motor vehicle to cross or enter a bike lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Outside those five legal exceptions, drifting or parking inside a bike lane violates Kentucky traffic rules.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Why are abrupt brake checks and surprise horn blasts dangerous around bicycle riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Car tires outstop narrow bike rims easily, and loud close blasts jolt riders into moving lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: When may a cyclist keep both hands on the bars instead of signaling, and what warns you?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Potholes or wobbles force two-hand control, making shoulder glances your earliest clue before a lane move.
sec10-card-sec10-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Rough spots grab bars, watch heads

visual_sync.text_span: Rough spots grab bars, watch heads

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Which highways bar bicycles, and how must cyclists ride regarding traffic flow and signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Riding with right-edge traffic flow and halting at red lights keeps cyclists predictable to motorists.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What night lamps, walker rules, and sidewalk or path rules apply to bicycle riders?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Unlit night bikes stay invisible until headlights strike them too late for a safe brake check.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: How many people may a bicycle carry, and how many riders may travel side by side?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Handlebar passengers wreck steering balance, and riding three wide blocks overtaking vehicles from passing safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: What weight, top speed, and minimum rider age define legal electric scooters on Kentucky roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Knowing scooter speed caps and bike-law status prepares drivers for twenty-mile-per-hour riders in city lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: During which hours must electric scooters run front and rear lights, and how may they park?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Sprawled scooters across sidewalks trap wheelchair users and blind pedestrians while dark scooters invite night strikes.
sec10-card-sec10-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Half-hour dusk to dawn, clear walks

visual_sync.text_span: Half-hour dusk to dawn, clear walks

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: How do a cyclist's legal duties on roadways combine with duties toward pedestrians and darkness?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Cyclists carry full vehicle duties on asphalt yet owe pedestrians priority and bright lamps after dark.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: What rider age minimum and nighttime lighting window govern electric scooters in Kentucky?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Test questions pair the sixteen-year rider threshold directly with the thirty-minute post-sunset and pre-sunrise lamp rule.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: How much lane width and dry-road following gap must you give a motorcycle ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Crowding half a bike's lane or tailgating steals swerve space when riders brake hard or lean.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Why do motorcyclists dart suddenly within their lane, and how fast do mopeds typically move?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Gravel patches, rail tracks, or pavement seams that cars barely feel can dump two wheels instantly.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Roughly how many car-truck crashes happen yearly, and what four traits set big rigs apart?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Assuming an eighteen-wheeler stops, sees, or turns like a sedan drives most preventable highway truck wrecks.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Which side of a tractor-trailer hides the largest blind spot, and what mirror check saves you?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Cruising beside a right-side trailer hides your roof completely if the trucker needs to swerve right.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: How far behind a large truck does its rear blind zone stretch, and how do hills affect rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Tailgating a trailer blinds both you and the trucker while steep grades slow heavy rigs dramatically.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: Why do trucks swing left before turning right, and where must you stop at intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Sneaking between a right-blinking trailer and the curb crushes your car as rear axles track inward.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What rules protect you around trucks at exits, runaway ramps, uphill queues, and rail crossings?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Parking on gravel runaway ramps or tailgating uphill rigs puts your hood under unstoppable rolling weight.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: What lane share and time cushion belong to every motorcycle in dry versus wet weather?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop fast on dry tar yet lose grip quickly in rain, demanding even wider cushions.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Which dangerous driver habits get punished inside a truck's side no-zones versus its front no-zone?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Pacing a trailer's flank invites sideswipes while diving close ahead erases the rig's braking cushion.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: How many feet of truck braking room sit ahead versus rear blind-spot length behind?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Memorizing three hundred thirty-five front feet and two hundred rear feet aces Kentucky's no-zone questions.
sec10-card-sec10-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Three thirty-five front, two hundred rear

visual_sync.text_span: Three thirty-five front, two hundred rear

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: How do turning trucks and oncoming cars share tight space when a rig turns right?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Giving oncoming or turning trailers extra centerline margin prevents sideswipes from forty-eight-foot trailer off-tracking.
sec10-card-sec10-R12.must_match_memory_hook: Rigs swing wide, cars hug right

visual_sync.text_span: Rigs swing wide, cars hug right

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: Why must passenger cars never cut off heavy trucks or stop near mountain escape ramps?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Escape ramps exist solely to catch brakeless commercial rigs hurtling downhill at highway speeds.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: How must you respond whenever a vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights or sirens?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection bottles up cross lanes right where an ambulance needs to turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Where must you hold during an emergency pass, and how close may you follow afterward?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Drafting closer than five hundred feet behind fire trucks risks colliding with second-responding units or hoses.
sec10-card-sec10-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Curbside stop, stay five hundred back

visual_sync.text_span: Curbside stop, stay five hundred back

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What calm steps should you take right after pulling over for a police traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Rummaging in gloveboxes as an officer walks up looks dangerous compared to calm hands on wheel.
sec10-card-sec10-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Engine off, cabin lit, hands visible

visual_sync.text_span: Engine off, cabin lit, hands visible

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: How should you retrieve documents, handle citations, and obey instructions during a police stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Arguing tickets on the shoulder solves nothing while fleeing turns a traffic citation into felony danger.
sec10-card-sec10-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Announce reaches, stay belted, never flee

visual_sync.text_span: Announce reaches, stay belted, never flee

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: How do you merge safely after a traffic stop ends, and why do move-over laws exist?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Roadside strikes maim troopers and tow crews every year when passing traffic fails to move over.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What must Kentucky drivers do on four-lane versus two-lane roads for shouldered emergency vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Shifting left on multi-lane highways or slowing carefully on two-lanes shields responders working feet from mirrors.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: What two rules govern pulling aside for sirens and trailing emergency vehicles down the road?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Permit questions love pairing immediate right-curb yielding with the strict five-hundred-foot following ban.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: Where do your hands belong when a stop begins, and when do you reach for papers?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Keeping both hands in plain view until asked removes tension for everyone on dark roadsides.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: How does your move-over response change when the adjacent lane is open versus blocked?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Forcing an unsafe lane change causes sideswipes, so slowing way down protects crews when boxed in.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: How should you pass horseback riders or animal-drawn vehicles on Kentucky rural roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Blasting a horn or gunning exhaust bolts startled horses sideways across your hood.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Where does Kentucky generally ban all-terrain vehicles from operating?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Low-pressure off-road tires handle poorly on pavement, so public roads allow ATVs only under strict exceptions.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: What landowner, helmet, supervision, and passenger rules bind ATV riders in Kentucky?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Unlicensed teen riders carrying passengers without helmets or adult supervision drive severe off-road rollovers.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: Under what angle, distance, license, lamp, and daylight limits may an ATV cross or work roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Crossing two-lane blacktop squarely under two tenths of a mile minimizes paved exposure.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: What speed defines orange-triangle slow vehicles, and what spooks horse-drawn rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Closing at fifty-five on an under-twenty-five farm rig shrinks gaps way faster than city drivers expect.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: What two baseline requirements and two-lane crossing limits govern Kentucky ATVs?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Knowing permission, approved headgear, ninety-degree angles, and two-tenths distance covers every ATV question cleanly.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: What lesson does the opening review item teach about how alcohol and drugs affect driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Distractor choices claim alcohol sharpens focus or speeds reactions when impairment always degrades safe decisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Who may pass when a dashed yellow line runs on your side of the center stripe?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Opposing traffic faces a solid yellow barrier while only your lane holds broken-line passing permission.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same instant?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Hesitating or surging left causes four-way fender-benders whenever drivers forget the car on the right.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Which background color identifies regulatory traffic signs rather than guide or warning signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Green marks directional guide boards and yellow signals warnings, leaving white for enforceable traffic rules.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: What must you do if a pedestrian jaywalks illegally across the middle of your street?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Having legal right-of-way never permits striking a person who steps mid-street across your path.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Which two false benefits do alcohol and drugs never give a driver behind the wheel?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: False confidence tricks impaired drivers into thinking dulled reflexes feel quicker than sober ones.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Does a broken yellow stripe on your side open passing for both directions or yours alone?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Each half of a double centerline speaks strictly to the lane bordering that stripe.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Which two wrong instincts fail when two cars arrive together at a four-way stop?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Barging straight ahead or yielding left breaks the universal rule giving priority to the right.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: What color tells you a roadside panel states a mandatory regulatory rule?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Spotting white backgrounds from afar primes you early for speed caps, lane rules, or turn bans.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Why are blasting the horn or brushing past wrong responses to a mid-street jaywalker?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Honking panics exposed pedestrians in mid-stride when clean braking prevents a life-altering collision.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: How much of a traffic lane belongs legally to a motorcycle operator?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Squeezing alongside a rider inside one lane steals the swerve room needed to dodge potholes.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How should motorists adjust speed and side room when overtaking a bicyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Rushing close past handlebars with horn blasts can startle a cyclist right under your mirror.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Which road conditions fit high-beam headlights, and which four situations forbid them?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: High beams help on clear open stretches yet blind followers and bounce glare off precipitation.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How does the Kentucky manual define driver distraction in plain terms?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Screens, snacks, or cabin drama all count whenever eyes, hands, or thoughts drift off traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Why must drivers never crowd a motorcycle into half a lane or onto the shoulder?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Every motorcyclist holds full single-lane vehicle status rather than leftover shoulder pavement.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Which two aggressive habits must drivers avoid whenever overtaking a cyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Patience behind a bicycle until an open gap clears beats a fast close brush every time.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: When does the review rule say to switch on high-beam headlights at night?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Scanning twice as far down empty dark pavement spots deer and curves well before low beams.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Which two warning signs do the handbook's graphic review items ask learners to identify?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Reading symbol shapes and arrows fast lets you spot upcoming medians and sharp bends without text.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: Where and how does the closing chapter let you grade all eleven rehearsal items?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Checking the eleven-letter footer key pinpoints weak chapters before you sit at the licensing counter.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Which three distraction research sources receive credit on the manual's closing page?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: National administrator, federal safety, and university crash research back every distraction rule in the book.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What publication year, Arlington organization, purpose, and artwork credits appear in the manual's imprint?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: The Arlington administrator imprint frames the booklet as a focused rules-and-signs study companion.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: What role do the eleven rehearsal items and footer key serve compared with licensing day?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Mastering eleven warm-up items previews format only, so full handbook study remains essential.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: How do the closing distraction citations differ from the manual's two thousand twenty-two imprint?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Research citations document distraction data whereas the publisher block identifies the two thousand twenty-two supplement.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What eyesight habits and nighttime eyewear rule does safe driving require?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Wearing dark sunglasses or tinted lenses after sunset cuts crucial night contrast when spotting dark hazards is hardest.
sec03-card-sec03-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Check eyes, wear lenses, skip tint

visual_sync.text_span: Check eyes, wear lenses, skip tint

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Which two visual abilities help you track side motion, hold lane position, and react to hazards?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Side vision catches cars creeping into adjacent lanes while depth perception tells you whether a passing or turn gap fits.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What traffic warnings do your ears catch, what should fading hearing prompt, and how do deaf drivers adapt?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Horns and ambulance sirens often reach your ears before flashing lights clear blind corners, unless trained eyes scan wider.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What pre-trip sleep target, road-break interval, passenger tip, and label check help beat highway fatigue?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Stopping every one hundred miles or two hours after a full night's rest keeps tunnel vision and slow reactions away.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: When drowsiness hits mid-drive, what action works better than rolling windows down or cranking music?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Cold air and loud radio tricks wear off fast?only pulling safely off the road for genuine sleep restores alertness.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: How can you pair caffeine with a brief rest stop, and what driving hours carry the highest fatigue risk?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Drinking caffeine right before a short nap lets alertness kick in as you wake, though avoiding late-night drives works best.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Into what three categories do driving distractions fall, and what everyday cabin habits trigger them?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Phones, burgers, or passenger debates pull your eyes off pavement, hands off the wheel, or focus off traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Why is texting uniquely dangerous, how long does it steal your eyes at 55 mph, and how much do handheld tasks multiply risk?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Looking down for four point six seconds at fifty-five miles per hour drives the length of an entire football field blindfolded.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: What four practical habits keep everyday distractions out of the driver's seat?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Muting notifications, skipping behind-the-wheel meals, avoiding heated arguments, and buckling kids and pets keeps attention forward.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How do healthy vision and sharp hearing complement each other behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Corrected eyesight measures lane gaps ahead while unobstructed ears pick up sirens and horns hidden behind buildings.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How does preventing fatigue before a road trip differ from handling sudden drowsiness mid-trip?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Seven to nine hours of sleep plus two-hour breaks prevent exhaustion, whereas yawning mid-drive demands an immediate twenty-minute nap.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: How does texting compare with single-channel cabin distractions?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Reading and typing a message steals your eyes, occupies your fingers, and hijacks your brain simultaneously.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What eye-opening statistic backs up Kentucky's plain cabin advice against phones, meals, and arguments?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Knowing one text blinds you for nearly five seconds makes silencing phones and skipping snacks non-negotiable.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: How do intense feelings like anger, worry, fear, excitement, or depression hurt your driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Mental replay of bad news or excitement crowds out split-second brake light and crosswalk scanning.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What five smart choices help an angry or upset person avoid driving dangerously?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Taking a walk, leaving early, shrugging off cutoffs, or letting a calm friend drive beats turning two tons of steel into a vent.
sec03-card-sec03-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Cool off, pad time, pass keys

visual_sync.text_span: Cool off, pad time, pass keys

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Where does Kentucky draw the legal line between aggressive driving and road rage?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Tailgating, speeding, and weaving draw traffic citations, whereas threatening or assaulting someone with a car crosses into violent crime.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What everyday style prevents road rage, and where should you go if an angry driver targets you?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Never lead a hostile driver to your driveway or trade gestures—head to a busy, well-lit lot and call police.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Which five warning signs tell an aging driver to seek an evaluation, and which board handles it?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Concerned family, getting lost on familiar streets, police warnings, recent fender-benders, or doctor advice call for a Medical Review Board check.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: In one sentence, what separates aggressive driving from full-blown road rage?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Permit questions test whether you spot criminal intent to harm or intimidate as the jump from aggressive driving to rage.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: How does handling your own anger before driving differ from responding to another driver's road rage?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: You defuse your own temper before turning the key, whereas facing someone else's rage means escaping to a lit public place and phoning police.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Roughly what share of fatal crashes involve alcohol or impairing drugs, and how much does it take to raise risk?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: You do not have to hit the legal limit to crash—every single drink or impairing pill tilts the odds against getting home.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Which three alcohol actions are completely illegal for anyone under 21?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance laws outlaw underage alcohol across the board long before anyone even reaches for car keys.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: At what drink or BAC point do judgment, eye tracking, color sense, and reaction speed start slipping?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Alcohol dulls self-control first, fooling buzzed drivers into thinking they feel sharp while vision already blurs at point zero two.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: Which common over-the-counter pills can impair driving, and what three precautions keep you safe?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Non-prescription cold, allergy, nerve, or stimulant tablets can sedate or jitter you dangerously—especially if mixed with alcohol.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Which four prescription drug families commonly dull reflexes and judgment, and whom should you consult?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Holding a doctor's prescription never shields you from a crash or DUI charge if painkillers or sleep aids impair your driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What fine, jail range, and license suspension hit a first illegal-drug driving conviction within ten years?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: First-offense drug-impaired driving brings two hundred to five hundred dollars plus fees, jail time, and up to four months suspended.
sec03-card-sec03-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Five-hundred fine, thirty jail, four-month loss

visual_sync.text_span: Five-hundred fine, thirty jail, four-month loss

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: How do pills compare with alcohol alone, and what happens when someone combines them?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: One drink plus one antihistamine or sedative compounds drowsiness far beyond adding their separate effects together.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How do Kentucky's numerical alcohol cutoffs compare with how drug-driving convictions are penalized?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Alcohol laws set clear zero-point-zero-eight adult and zero-point-zero-two youth thresholds, while drug convictions trigger fines, jail, and multi-month suspensions.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: What BAC thresholds define Kentucky DUI for adults and under-21 drivers, and can you be convicted below 0.08?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Blowing under point zero eight never guarantees walking free if weaving or failed field checks prove impairing influence.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which three chemical checks does implied consent cover, and what three consequences follow refusing one?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Refusing an officer's test costs your license immediately, enters court against you, and doubles mandatory jail if convicted.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: After completing police chemical testing, what independent test right does a driver have?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Once you submit to the officer's required test, you may hire a qualified doctor, nurse, phlebotomist, or tech for a second blood sample.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: How soon may a DUI-suspended driver apply for an interlock license, and how long does an arrestee get to try reaching a lawyer?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Arrestees get a brief ten-to-fifteen-minute window to phone counsel before testing, and interlock time earns credit toward suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What fines, jail time, and suspension span apply to a first alcohol DUI conviction inside ten years?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: First-time alcohol offenders face up to five hundred dollars plus court costs, up to thirty days jailed, and months suspended.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: Which six aggravating factors lock in mandatory jail time on a Kentucky DUI?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Speeding thirty over, driving wrong-way, causing serious injury or death, blowing point one five, refusing tests, or carrying a child under twelve mandates jail.
sec03-card-sec03-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty over, wrong-way, crash, refusal, kid

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty over, wrong-way, crash, refusal, kid

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: What happens to your license plates during a DUI suspension without an interlock or hardship permit, and what BAC blocks an interlock start?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Without an approved ignition interlock or hardship permit, courts impound tags, and blowing above point zero two locks the starter.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: What big sentencing jump separates an aggravated first DUI from a non-aggravated first DUI?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: While any first DUI suspends your license for months, adding high speed, point one five BAC, refusal, or a young child locks in mandatory jail.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Before driving on a highway, where must a Kentucky vehicle be registered, and how many days do buyers or new residents get?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Buying a car or moving one into Kentucky starts a strict fifteen-day filing clock at your home county clerk's office.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Does Kentucky offer a registration grace period, when are reminder notices mailed, and does missing the mail excuse you?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Blaming a lost forty-five-day postcard never waives expired-tag penalties once your registration date passes.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What happens to your registration, wallet, and freedom if you drive uninsured in Kentucky?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Driving without coverage is a criminal offense carrying five hundred to one thousand dollars in fines and up to ninety days jailed.
sec02-card-sec02-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Revoked tag, thousand fine, ninety-day jail

visual_sync.text_span: Revoked tag, thousand fine, ninety-day jail

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: What are Kentucky's minimum liability insurance amounts under both split-limit and single-limit policies?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Carrying at least twenty-five/fifty/twenty-five split coverage—or one sixty-thousand-dollar combined pool—keeps your registration legal.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which mandatory benefit covers every insured vehicle except motorcycles, and how may you carry proof in the car?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Keeping an active insurance card printed in the glovebox or ready on your phone satisfies roadside verification.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: How do college students in Kentucky, Kentucky students studying away, and stationed military members handle tags and insurance?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Enrolled visitors pair home registration with a Kentucky college ID, while military members can title locally using out-of-state policies.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: How should active-duty service members clear a mistaken uninsured notice triggered by out-of-state coverage?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Presenting active-duty verification to the county clerk keeps automated insurance checks from canceling a valid military registration.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: What two steps must happen before driving on a highway, and when does the 15-day clerk deadline apply?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Every highway mile requires county-clerk application and active insurance, with fifteen days allowed to formalize newly bought or moved-in cars.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: How does a 25/50/25 split liability policy structure coverage differently from a $60,000 single-limit policy?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Split policies divide separate caps for one injury, total injuries, and property damage, whereas sixty thousand covers all crash claims together.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How do visiting college students and stationed military members differ on Kentucky vehicle titling and insurance?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Students roll on home-state plates beside a campus ID, while stationed troops can hold a Kentucky title backed by out-of-state insurance.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: How do State Police support testers with disabilities, and which specialists serve on the Medical Review Board?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Eye, nerve, mental-health, and rehabilitation doctors review complex cases so capable drivers get fair accommodations.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: How many episode-free days must someone wait to drive after a seizure or blackout, and how is it verified?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Blacking out behind the wheel causes unbraked high-speed wrecks, so Kentucky requires ninety clear days sworn by affidavit.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What best-eye acuity score plus horizontal and vertical field-of-view angles meet Kentucky's legal vision floor?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Sharp straight-ahead reading is useless without thirty-five-degree side and twenty-five-degree vertical peripheral awareness at intersections.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: What vision scores, visual field, and training agency qualify a driver for Kentucky's bioptic telescopic lens program?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Drivers with stable twenty-over-two-hundred eyes reaching twenty-over-sixty through a bioptic scope train through Vocational Rehabilitation.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: What four referral sources can send a driver to the Medical Review Board, and how is the final ruling delivered?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Once referred, drivers submit physician forms so the board can evaluate fitness and mail back a written decision.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: How does Kentucky's medical rule for seizures and blackouts differ from its legal eyesight standard?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Episode disorders track a ninety-day calendar wait, whereas vision testing measures twenty-over-sixty sharpness and peripheral angles.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How does a standard driver's vision floor compare with a bioptic applicant's starting eye score and scope target?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Both paths demand twenty-over-sixty clarity to read signs, whether achieved naturally with glasses or magnified through a bioptic scope.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How do reporting rules to the Medical Review Board differ between public or medical officials and private citizens?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Requiring two citizens to sign a sworn affidavit prevents lone grudge reports while still letting doctors, judges, or sheriffs act directly.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: Which groups suffer most from vehicle-fed ground ozone, and what three habits cut exhaust pollution?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Tuned engines, gentle throttle habits, and combined errands slash lung-irritating smog that hits kids, seniors, and outdoor crews hardest.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: At which two licensing moments can Kentuckians join the organ-donor registry?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Adding donor status right when you get or renew your card records your lifesaving choice cleanly on your credential.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: How should your back, feet, wheel height, chest gap, and head restraint line up in the driver's seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Sitting upright ten inches back with the headrest above ear height lets belts, airbags, and whiplash guards protect your spine.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: How do you aim your inside rearview mirror and lean-set your outside mirrors, and how many degrees of view does that add?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Pushing side mirrors outward until your own fenders disappear widens coverage twelve to sixteen degrees per side into blind zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: What five cleaning steps keep vehicle glass clear, and what three items are banned from obstructing windshields?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Dangling mirror charms, windshield decals, interior smoke film, or illegal dark tint create deadly blind spots right across crosswalks.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How often and against what label do you check tire pressure, and how does the Lincoln penny test check tread?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Seeing the very top of Lincoln's head upside down in a groove means your tires have worn dangerously bald.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: Which two tire checks and three seating benchmarks belong in a driver's pre-drive setup?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Pairing grippy inflated tires underneath with a ten-inch upright posture inside prepares both car and driver before rolling.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does your target view in the center rearview mirror differ from properly lean-set side mirrors?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Seeing your own doors in side mirrors duplicates what the center mirror already shows while leaving adjacent lanes hidden.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: What two baseline requirements keep both your windshield legal and every person inside legal?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Uncluttered glass lets you spot hazards early while fastened belts on every rider protect everyone if someone else crashes into you.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Who must wear proper restraints in post-1981 vehicles in Kentucky, and what two crash benefits do belts deliver?
