sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Fastened belts keep every passenger inside the steel safety cage and hold the driver behind the wheel to steer.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: Can Kentucky police pull you over solely for an unbuckled seat belt, and how must shoulder and lap straps sit?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Officers need zero other violation to write a belt ticket, and slipping the strap under an arm risks severe rib trauma.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: How fast do airbags fire in moderate-to-severe crashes, what harmless puff appears, and why must belts stay buckled?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Harmless deployment powder looks like smoke, and because airbags only back up front hits once, belts remain essential.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: To stay safe around airbags, where belong your seat, hands, dashboard items, and children aged 12 and under?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Loose phones or cups on the dash turn into shrapnel when a bag fires, and kids twelve and under belong belted in back.
sec04-card-sec04-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Slide back, clear dash, kids rear

visual_sync.text_span: Slide back, clear dash, kids rear

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: May a rear-facing infant seat ever sit in front of an active passenger airbag, and how may one be turned off?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: An inflating front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing carrier right behind an infant's head with lethal force.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does a seat belt's protection across maneuvers and multi-hit crashes differ from an airbag's?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Airbags deflate immediately after the first impact, leaving only your seat belt to hold you through rollovers or second hits.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Which children by height must ride in a federally approved child restraint, and what fine-plus-fee hits violators?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Skipping a federal car seat for a child forty inches or under draws a fifty-dollar fine plus a ten-dollar brain-injury fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: What age and height range requires a booster seat in Kentucky, and what height graduates out regardless of age?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Children under eight standing between forty and fifty-seven inches need a booster lift so adult belts fit hips and collarbones.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Where is the safest spot to anchor a child seat, who checks installations free, and what unattended-child crime applies under age 8?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Middle-rear placement maximizes side-impact buffer, State Police inspect seats, and fatally leaving a child under eight unattended is a felony.
sec04-card-sec04-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Center rear, troopers check, never leave

visual_sync.text_span: Center rear, troopers check, never leave

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: How does Kentucky's height cutoff for a full child safety restraint separate from its booster-seat band?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Forty inches marks the handoff from full harnessed child seats into the forty-to-fifty-seven-inch booster zone for kids under eight.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: Under Kentucky rules, what five unwanted movements must be impossible before a cargo load counts as secure?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: If gravel can sift out or lumber can slide forward on hard braking, your load is legally unsecured.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: What gear secures cargo, why must loads and pets get rechecked, and whose view must high loads never block?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Bumps loosen straps mid-trip, unrestrained pets distract or fly forward on braking, and towering loads blind trailing drivers.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: What are the limits of driver-assist tech on road checks and daily drives, and what three upkeep habits keep it working?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Examiners restrict assist features during road checks, and dirty cameras, outdated software, or zoned-out drivers defeat safety tech.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: What single standard makes cargo truly secure, and what single standard makes driver-assist technology safe?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Straps only work when nothing budges, and electronic alerts only save crashes when an attentive human stays in command.
sec04-card-sec04-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Zero cargo shift, full driver focus

visual_sync.text_span: Zero cargo shift, full driver focus

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: How far ahead must you signal an intersection turn in Kentucky, and should you copy a lead car's blinker blindly?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Signaling at least one hundred feet early warns followers, while blindly copying leaders causes wrong turns.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which lane edges launch right and left turns, and what lane rule governs multi-lane turns?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Swinging wide left before turning right—or drifting across dual turn stripes mid-corner—clips neighboring fenders.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: When is a driveway turnabout appropriate, and what clear sight distance must exist both ways first?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Without five hundred feet of clear sight each way, cresting cars reach you mid-reverse.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: How do you steer and align your vehicle while backing into a driveway for a turnabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Backing into the side drive lets you pull forward into main-road traffic afterward with full visibility.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Which four steps complete a driveway turnabout cleanly for Kentucky's road-skills exam?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Examiners grade turnabouts closely—check both directions twice before signaling left and accelerating smoothly.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: From which lane edges do right turns versus left turns launch?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Positioning tight to your turn side closes the gap where impatient cyclists or cars might squeeze.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How does car placement during a driveway turnabout differ from stopping on a two-lane road?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Centering inside the apron clears driveway posts while hugging right on unmarked asphalt protects opposing space.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: What five elements should you scan approaching any intersection, and whom can you assume will yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Assuming cross-street strangers will obey stop signs gets defensive drivers hit—verify wheel speed instead.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What head-check pattern follows a full stop, and what two checks precede rolling on a fresh green?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Waiting a beat on fresh green catches late red-light runners while confirming enough space across.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How should you handle buildings, parked rows, or tall trucks blocking your side view at a corner?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Poking your front bumper blindly into a live adjacent lane invites a high-speed broadside clip.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Why should you never pull out in front of an approaching car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Forgotten blinkers or drivers aiming for a driveway past yours cause classic pull-out T-bone crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which direction do Kentucky roundabouts circulate, who yields at entry, and what must you do when exiting?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Yielding to traffic already circling the island and signaling right before your exit keeps traffic flowing.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Which two bus types trigger mandatory stops when loading or unloading, and when may you move again?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Kentucky protects both school and church bus riders—hold still until children clear and wheels roll.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What is the single roadway setup where oncoming traffic need not stop for a flashing school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Plain painted center turn lanes never excuse oncoming traffic—only raised barriers or unpaved medians on four-plus lanes do.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Why do both a brand-new green light and a cross street's red light still demand visual checks?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Colored bulbs never build an invisible wall—scanning both ways catches distracted cross-street drivers.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Who must stop for a flashing school bus on two-lane or painted-median roads versus barrier-split four-lane highways?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Kids never cross concrete highway medians, which is why only opposite-direction divided four-lane traffic rolls on.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Where does legal parking belong, and what three steps open a perpendicular stall entry?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Respecting painted curbs and signaling before turning into a ninety-degree bay warns trailing aisle traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How far straight back must you creep from a perpendicular space before turning the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Cranking the wheel too early swings your front corner sideways into the parked car beside you.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: When backing into a parallel curb space, what bumper-to-bumper landmark signals quick counter-steering?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Counter-steering once your nose clears their rear bumper tucks your car cleanly beside the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Once centered in a parallel spot, which side should you exit when safe, and what three lockup steps does law mandate?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Kentucky law forbids leaving an idling, unlocked car with keys inside—shut off, pull keys, and lock.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: When pulling out of a parallel space for your skills test, what cabin landmark must clear the lead car's rear bumper?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Waiting until your door pillar clears their bumper guarantees your rear quarter panel won't scrape.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How do you angle parked wheels on hills with versus without curbs, even during a brief errand?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Aiming tires into a curb—or toward the ditch where curbless—keeps rollaways out of live lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Who may legally park in handicapped bays, and which Kentucky office issues disability plates or decals?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's placard when that disabled rider isn't aboard still draws a parking fine.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: How does your front bumper's cue differ between backing out of a ninety-degree bay and backing into parallel?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Both maneuvers hinge on watching your front bumper against neighboring cars so nothing scrapes.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: How do hill wheel angles combine with Kentucky's mandatory unattended-vehicle lockup steps?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Turned front tires back up your parking brake while removing keys and locking obeys state statute.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: How are three-lane highways organized by speed and move—and what left-lane habit is illegal on limited-access highways?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Cruising continuously in a freeway's left passing lane clogs traffic and violates Kentucky law.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: Which lane must your turn finish in, and how should you handle missing a turn or entering a turn lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Jerking across lanes mid-intersection causes broadside crashes—follow through calmly and loop at the next block.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Which two visual checks open every safe lane change before you move over?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Mirrors spot fast-closing traffic back while your over-the-shoulder glance clears the adjacent fender pocket.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: After checking mirrors and blind spots, what four actions complete a smooth lane change?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Matching target-lane pace before gliding over keeps trailing drivers from slamming their brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: How do you merge from an acceleration lane onto a freeway, and who holds right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Stopping or creeping slowly off an entrance ramp forces seventy-mile-per-hour traffic into emergency swerves.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: When exiting a freeway, where must you maintain normal speed and where should braking begin?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Braking early on live interstate lanes invites high-speed rear-end crashes—wait for the deceleration lane.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: How does lane assignment shift between a three-plus-lane road and a two-lane same-way road?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Keeping through traffic centered or right leaves the leftmost lane open for brisk passing.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What is the right play when you miss your turn versus once you commit to a turn lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Two extra minutes circling the next corner beats risking a side-impact wreck with a panicked swerve.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: How do acceleration lanes and deceleration lanes handle highway speed transitions oppositely?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Both ramps exist so speed changes happen off the main freeway lanes rather than inside fast flow.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Which side handles normal passing, and under what rare condition may you leave pavement to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Right-side blind zones surprise drivers—never touch unpaved shoulders unless bypassing a fully halted car safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: How do broken-and-solid yellow centerlines govern passing, and within what oncoming footage must you finish?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Kentucky sets a two-hundred-foot oncoming buffer—plus finishing before any solid-yellow no-passing zone begins.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: During a brisk left pass, what mirror sight tells you enough room exists to signal back right?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Waiting until both headlights of the passed car appear in your center mirror prevents clipping bumpers.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: Why must you never start a pass on blind hills or curves, or near crossroads, schools, and shops?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Assume every blind crest hides an oncoming truck while busy storefronts launch surprise left-turners.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: How much lateral space do bicycles and scooters get when you pass—and may you cross a no-passing stripe?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Kentucky lets you cross even a solid centerline when clear ahead to give cyclists three safe feet.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What does Kentucky law require of you when another vehicle pulls out to pass your car?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Speeding up to trap a passer in opposing traffic is illegal and risks a head-on wreck.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Between a solid yellow stripe and a broken yellow stripe, how do you know whether your side may pass?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Solid paint right beside your left tires forbids passing, while broken dashes on your side allow it.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: How does your clearance rule when passing a car compare with passing a cyclist?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Wind blast from a close pass can knock a cyclist down—give three feet or a whole lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What do right-of-way laws actually establish, and does any driver ever own right-of-way automatically?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn against a red-light runner causes crashes—every intersection requires reading live traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Who yields at a staggered stop, on a left turn, and when two cars reach a four-way stop together?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Remembering that oncoming right-turners also beat your left turn avoids classic corner fender-benders.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Who yields when pulling from a driveway, minor street, or freeway ramp—and who wins inside an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Traffic already rolling on main roads or still clearing the intersection always holds priority over newcomers.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Across signals, signs, lane paint, crews, guards, and police officers, whose command overrides everything else?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Even if a signal shines green, an officer waving you to halt holds supreme legal command.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How does arrival order decide four-way stops, and what breaks an exact tie?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Yielding to the car on your right clears simultaneous arrivals smoothly without hesitation.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: How are red, yellow, and green lenses arranged on vertical versus horizontal traffic signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Consistent lamp positions let color-blind drivers read every intersection signal reliably day or night.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What must you yield to on a circular green light, especially before turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: A plain green ball gives unprotected left turns—charging across oncoming through lanes causes T-bone wrecks.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What does a steady yellow signal require, and where does Kentucky draw the line on red-light violations?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Clearing out after entering on yellow is lawful, whereas crossing the stop line after red breaks law.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Where must you halt on a steady red light, and when is turning right on red allowed?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Rolling past the crosswalk without halting first earns a red-light ticket even when right turns are allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Under what sole street-type pairing may you turn left on red, and into which lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Turning left on red onto or from a two-way street crosses opposing lanes illegally.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What different actions do a flashing yellow light and a flashing red light command?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Treat flashing red just like a stop sign while easing speed alertly through flashing yellow zones.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What must you do at twin flashing red railroad lights, and how do you treat a plain crossbuck?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Pulling across while red railroad lamps still flash violates law even if one train cleared.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: How do steady green, flashing yellow, upward green, and steady red arrows direct your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Always obey the signal head mounted directly over your own lane—red arrows forbid turning completely.
sec06-card-sec06-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Green goes, yellow yields, red bans

visual_sync.text_span: Green goes, yellow yields, red bans

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How does a steady yellow traffic light differ in meaning from a flashing yellow beacon?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Confusing steady yellow for mere caution tempts late entries right as cross traffic gets green.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: What separates a flashing yellow beacon's rule from a flashing red beacon's rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Rolling through a flashing red without halting wheels completely counts as running a stop sign.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: After a legal full stop, how is right-on-red broader than left-on-red?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Keep that contrast sharp on test day—left on red never works if either street carries two-way traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How does protection change when a steady green turn arrow switches to a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Oncoming traffic holds green during your flashing yellow arrow, demanding a clear gap before turning.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: What does the round yellow railroad sign warn you to do ahead of the white crossbuck?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Slowing at the round yellow disc ensures you can stop behind the white line before the crossbuck.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Why must you visually check every rail in both directions even if no track-count plaque or lights appear?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Not every multi-track crossing posts a number plaque or flashing gates, leaving visual scanning on you.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How should you cross clear railroad tracks, and where must you wait if traffic backs up ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Stopping on steel rails behind backed-up cars leaves zero escape if crossing gates drop.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: If your car stalls on railroad tracks, which direction do you run and whom do you call?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Running forty-five degrees toward the approaching locomotive keeps derailed wreckage flying past behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: How far can a fifty-five-mile-per-hour freight train roll before stopping, and why wait after one clears?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: A caboose clearing track one can hide a second fast locomotive barreling down track two.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: What mindset belongs at every railroad crossing, and what happens if you drive around lowered gates?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Weaving around crossing arms or ignoring flashing reds is an automatic traffic citation—and often fatal.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How does the round yellow railroad board's role differ from the white crossbuck's stop rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Advance yellow discs prep your foot early so you halt cleanly before the crossbuck stop line.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What shape and colors mark standard warning boards, and where does fluorescent yellow-green appear?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: High-visibility fluorescent yellow-green pops out in dawn glare around schools and pedestrian crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: What color marks construction and maintenance zones, and which temporary controls must you obey inside them?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Shifting pavement, slow graders, and live crews mean flagger paddles and white stop lines rule.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How do you protect highway crews in work zones, and what penalty hits work-zone speeders?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Kentucky doubles speeding fines in highway work zones because cones offer zero armor to workers.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What colors mark regulatory boards, what does a red circle-and-slash mean, and what condition caps speed limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Posted black-and-white speed numbers apply strictly to ideal dry conditions—storms require dropping lower.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: How do the eight-sided stop board and downward-pointing triangle yield board differ in shape and duty?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Unique silhouettes let you recognize a stop octagon or yield triangle even from the back.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What are shared center turn lanes limited to, and what do wrong-way and do-not-enter boards guard?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Using a center turn strip for passing or ignoring red wrong-way boards invites head-on crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What separates the physical requirement of an eight-sided red board from a red-and-white triangle?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: A yield triangle allows rolling carefully when clear, whereas a stop octagon requires zero wheel motion.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: How do white boards, yellow diamonds, and green-brown-blue boards divide roadway messages?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Sorting background color instantly tells your brain whether a rule is mandatory, cautionary, or directional.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Which destinations do green, brown, and blue square or rectangular guide boards point toward?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Green directs highway exits, brown highlights parks and historic sites, and blue marks motorist services.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: What do highway route shields identify, and how should you prepare before driving unfamiliar territory?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Studying numbered interstate and state shields beforehand beats reading tiny street names at highway speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: Which five traffic-organization jobs do painted road lines, arrows, words, and symbols handle?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Roadway paint carries full legal force just like post-mounted signs for lane discipline and stopping.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Where do you halt when a stop line precedes a crosswalk—and what if an intersection lacks painted lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Many legal corner crossings carry zero white paint, so always stop short of the intersection box.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: On standard traffic boards, what do red, green, and yellow backgrounds communicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Reading background color from a block away preps your foot before lettering even comes into focus.
sec06-card-sec06-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Red forbids, green guides, yellow warns

visual_sync.text_span: Red forbids, green guides, yellow warns

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: What messages belong to horizontal rectangles, triangles, vertical rectangles, diamonds, pentagons, and round boards?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Snow or mud crusting a board face never hides a five-sided school pentagon or round rail disc.
sec06-card-sec06-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Guide, yield, law, hazard, school, rail

visual_sync.text_span: Guide, yield, law, hazard, school, rail

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Which four distinct silhouettes announce yield, hazards, schools, and railroad crossings?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Recognizing those four silhouettes from a distance guarantees easy points on shape-recognition permit questions.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: How do red, green, and yellow divide prohibition, permission, and caution on road boards?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: From signals to signboards, those three colors carry identical meanings across every American roadway.
sec06-card-sec06-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Red stops, green permits, yellow warns

visual_sync.text_span: Red stops, green permits, yellow warns

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Which Kentucky license letters cover everyday cars, mopeds only, motorcycles, and commercial rigs?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Grabbing the wrong class letter stalls your application before a single road or written check begins.
sec01-card-sec01-F01.must_match_memory_hook: D car, E moped, M bike

visual_sync.text_span: D car, E moped, M bike

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: How do weight ratings, trailer limits, hazmat placards, and passenger seats divide CDL Classes A, B, and C?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Crossing twenty-six thousand one pounds or towing past ten thousand flips a commercial rig between Class A and Class B.
sec01-card-sec01-F02.must_match_memory_hook: A heavy tow, B heavy, C

visual_sync.text_span: A heavy tow, B heavy, C

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Do volunteer church or school bus drivers need a CDL, and which five vehicle uses are exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Unpaid bus seats still fall under commercial rules, unlike campers, military rigs, or farm trucks within one hundred fifty miles.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Who qualifies to apply for a Kentucky Class D license, which groups are exempt, and who is barred?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Fifteen-year-old residents need a parent signature below eighteen and three passed checks, while suspended or underage applicants are turned away.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What four mechanical caps define a Kentucky moped, and how can a 16-year-old earn a Class E license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Exceeding two horsepower, fifty cubic centimeters, or thirty miles per hour bumps a scooter out of moped rules into motorcycle territory.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What visibility and helmet guidance applies on a moped, and which highways are off-limits?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: A thirty-mile-per-hour moped cannot keep pace safely on limited-access highways where minimum speeds exceed its top end.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What wheel and seating setup defines a motorcycle, where may unlicensed minibikes ride, and how does the permit path work?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Riding a minibike onto public asphalt without credentials draws citations, while legal street riders earn a Class M via road check or RideSmartKY.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What perk do rider-course graduates get, and in what exact step order do State Police applicants test?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Finishing an approved rider class waives motorcycle testing, whereas standard applicants clear vision first before touching the written screen.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: Which three Kentucky license letters cover non-commercial driving, and which three cover commercial tiers?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Sorting everyday cars, mopeds, and motorcycles away from heavy freight and bus tiers keeps license classes crystal clear.
sec01-card-sec01-R01.must_match_memory_hook: D E M civilian, A-B-C pro

visual_sync.text_span: D E M civilian, A-B-C pro

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Which first-time Kentucky license class skips the behind-the-wheel skills exam completely?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Only moped-only Class E stops after vision and knowledge, while cars, motorcycles, and commercial rigs require live road evaluation.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: What must a parent or legal guardian bring and sign at the site for an applicant under 18?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Accepting joint financial responsibility in person beside a birth certificate or court order is mandatory before any minor tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What three licensing phases do Kentucky teens progress through, and what power does a signing parent keep?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Graduated licensing builds road skill step by step, and withdrawing parental consent cancels a minor's card immediately.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Which original documents must a teen permit seeker bring, how does residency proof change for REAL ID, and are copies allowed?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Showing up with a photocopy of your birth certificate, Social Security card, or school compliance form sends you home empty-handed.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: What hold period, practice hours, supervisor rule, passenger cap, and night curfew govern under-21 Kentucky permit holders?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Logging fifty daytime and ten nighttime hours beside a twenty-one-plus front passenger builds habits while limiting teen crash triggers.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: What alcohol cutoff, 180-day clock penalty, and minor point threshold apply to under-21 permit holders?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: One speeding or passenger ticket wipes out months of waiting by restarting your one-hundred-eighty-day countdown from zero.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: When may a teen book the State Police road check, what must they bring, may they drive there solo, and how long is a retry wait?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Driving yourself solo to the exam station breaks permit law before you start, and an expired eligibility letter cancels your slot.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: What credential do you earn on passing the teen road check, what unlocks full licensing, and what excuses midnight-to-6 driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Late-night solo trips between midnight and six stay off-limits unless backed by work, school, or an emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which four safety limits continue to apply to intermediate license holders under 18?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Earning solo privileges never lifts the one-unrelated-teen passenger cap, point zero two BAC rule, or clock-reset penalty.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Where do teens upgrade to a full license, by what age must driver training finish, and what four course paths count?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Skipping approved state, online, high-school, or private four-hour driver education past age nineteen blocks your unrestricted card.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: In what two ways do completed driver-education courses get reported to Kentucky licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: When a provider does not transmit electronically within two business days, mailing your certificate with name, birth date, and license number clears your record.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: What milestone does the first 180-day hold unlock, and what milestone does the second 180-day hold unlock?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Kentucky splits teen experience into two distinct half-year stretches—supervised practice first, then restricted solo driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What document rules, permit term, hold duration, and passenger requirement apply to new applicants aged 18 to 20?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Turning eighteen waives parental sign-off, yet young adults still practice half a year with an older licensed supervisor.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: How long must a new driver aged 21 or older hold a permit before road testing, and what car and retry rules apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Applicants twenty-one and up cut the permit wait down to thirty days, though road checks still demand an insured car, escort, and seven-day retry gap.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: What first-time vision score passes directly, what floor applies after a specialist referral, and what does the written check cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Needing glasses or contacts to hit twenty over forty adds a corrective-lens restriction code to your card.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What minimum percentage passes the Kentucky operator written exam, and in what formats is it available?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Missing more than one question in five drops you below eighty percent, whether testing on a tablet, orally, or in another language.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What paperwork and equipment does a State Police examiner inspect first, and what cabin rules govern the ride?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Examiners ride belted in a clean passenger seat giving plain commands without trick traps or third-party translators.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What visibility distances must high beams, low beams, and red taillights meet on a road-test car, and what cancels the check?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Showing up with illegal tint, missing plate lights, dead wipers, or weak beams cancels your appointment on the spot.
sec01-card-sec01-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Three-fifty high, one-hundred low, five-hundred rear

visual_sync.text_span: Three-fifty high, one-hundred low, five-hundred rear

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Which maneuvers get graded on the road check, what triggers an instant fail, and how many ignored instructions disqualify you?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: One traffic violation or bump ends the ride immediately, and ignoring an examiner's direction twice triggers automatic failure plus a one-week wait.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: When and how do State Police testing appointments open, and what must applicants needing accommodations do first?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Walk-ins get turned away at appointment-only sites, and interpreter or disability requests need a phone call before booking.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does passing the Kentucky written exam differ from passing the road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Answering rules questions hits a numeric eighty-percent bar, whereas road evaluation depends on safe live execution beside an examiner.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: On the road skills check, how does the strike limit for a dangerous act compare with ignoring examiner instructions?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Breaking a law or risking a crash allows zero second chances, while missed spoken directions allow one warning before disqualification.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: How soon must new Kentucky residents transfer a license, when must they retest, and how are out-of-state permits handled?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Valid out-of-state cards transfer without testing inside thirty days, while teen newcomers at fifteen-plus swap into a Kentucky permit first.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: What licensing rules cover out-of-state college students, non-citizens with foreign licenses, and permanent residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Carrying a Kentucky college ID lets full-time students drive on valid home-state plastic, while reciprocity gives foreign visitors up to a year.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: What determines how many exams international-permit holders take, and what waives exams for both resident classes?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Holding an intact license from another US state excuses testing, while unlicensed newcomers start at square one with a Kentucky permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: How can stationed military members renew a Kentucky Class D license away from home or reclaim an expired one after returning?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Returning service members get ninety days back in Kentucky to renew an expired card without sitting for exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: When do under-21 and adult licenses expire, how early can you renew, and what lapse triggers full retesting?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Adult four- or eight-year cards stay renewable test-free until five years expired, while under-twenty-one cards expire ninety days past twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: How quickly must you get a duplicate card after moving or changing your name, and how is a Social Security card treated?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Waiting past ten days risks a citation, and name changes require a legal marriage or court paper alongside—not replaced by—your updated Social Security card.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How does Kentucky's 30-day license transfer deadline treat permanent new residents differently from college students?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Establishing residency triggers the thirty-day transfer clock, whereas enrolled students keeping home-state residency just carry their campus ID.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How do exam rules for civilians holding international permits compare with troops returning from duty?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Country-by-country reciprocity sets civilian exam steps, whereas returning military personnel reclaim expired Class D privileges exam-free inside ninety days.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does the adult birthday renewal window compare with the deadline to update a changed name or address?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Mixing up those two clocks gets drivers ticketed when they assume moving houses gives a full month like birthdays do.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: Which serious offenses strip a license, how can parents or drivers end one voluntarily, and when do unpaid crash judgments suspend?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: DUI, test refusal, hit-and-run, fleeing, uninsured driving, or leaving a crash judgment unpaid past sixty days shuts down driving rights.
sec01-card-sec01-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Grave crimes, parent cancel, sixty-day debt

visual_sync.text_span: Grave crimes, parent cancel, sixty-day debt

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: At how many points inside two years do adults and under-18 drivers face suspension, and what does skipping the hearing cost?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Ignoring a point-hearing notice triggers automatic six-month, one-year, and two-year suspensions, and convictions linger five years on your record.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: How often can a point hearing swap suspension for probation, and how often may court-referred drivers attend state traffic school?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Failing to finish court-ordered state traffic school turns a minor ticket break right back into a license suspension.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: What mandatory assessment, program, fees, and wait stand between every DUI conviction and getting a license back?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Even after your suspension calendar runs out, Kentucky withholds reissue until cabinet assessment and education completion clear.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How do grave traffic crimes differ from routine moving violations in triggering a Kentucky suspension?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: One DUI or hit-and-run suspends immediately, whereas minor speeding tickets build toward twelve adult or seven minor points.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does eligibility for state traffic school differ from Kentucky's mandatory DUI education program?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Courts optionally refer minor moving tickets to traffic school once a year, whereas every single DUI conviction mandates cabinet treatment.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Why does driving at night carry greater difficulty and danger than driving in daylight?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlight beams leaves zero braking feet when an unlit hazard looms out of darkness.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: When do high beams help or hurt, and at what exact distances must you dim them?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Blasting high beams into fog or oncoming windshields blinds everyone with reflected glare.
sec11-card-sec11-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Where should you look against oncoming glare, and how much extra following time does night require?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Staring into oncoming brights bleaches your night vision while unfamiliar dark roads demand extra following cushion.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How far do high beams reach compared to lows, and when must you switch to low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: High beams double empty-road visibility yet bounce straight back off raindrops, snowflakes, and fog banks.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How do your eye aim in glare and your following gap on familiar versus strange night roads work?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Guiding off the white edge line preserves night sight while extra seconds absorb hidden curves.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: What intersection rights does an escorted funeral procession hold, and who still outranks it?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Cutting between escorted funeral cars causes multi-car intersection T-bones with drivers legally holding right-of-way.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Which multi-lane highways allow passing a funeral procession, and what penalties hit violators?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Illegally overtaking or breaking into a Kentucky funeral line risks hundreds in fines or jail time.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Why must you slow inside every work zone, and what triggers doubled fines in Kentucky?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Narrow barrels and grooved pavement stay hazardous when empty, and one worker doubles posted fines.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: How should you drive through an active work zone until passing the End Road Work sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes dominate construction corridors when impatient drivers tailgate ahead of sudden flagger stops.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Which three authorities or hazards still require an escorted funeral column to yield?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Even flashing escort vehicles must halt for emergency responders, officer hand signals, and locomotives.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Under which three exceptions may you overtake a funeral procession, and what penalty guards the rule?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: City street passing stays illegal without police direction, carrying two hundred fifty dollars or ninety days.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How does your speed duty in an empty work zone compare with Kentucky's doubled-fine trigger?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Empty cones still guard drop-offs and shifts, while signed zones with one worker double fines.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: How must you adjust speed and lane position on loose gravel versus narrow ditch-lined rural strips?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Loose stones lengthen every stop while steep roadside ditches punish tires hugging soft shoulders.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when two vehicles approach a narrow or single-lane rural bridge?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Racing an oncoming pickup onto a one-lane span leaves nowhere to swerve between steel guardrails.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: How should you handle open-grate bridge decks, blind wooded curves, and unmarked rural intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Wet steel grates wiggle tires sideways while tall cornrows hide crossroad pickups until the corner.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What seating, controls, belts, and wheel count define an autocycle under Kentucky rules?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Car-style seats, foot pedals, and three-point belts separate autocycles from straddle-seat three-wheel motorcycles.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Which traffic rules apply to autocycles, and do drivers need a motorcycle endorsement or helmet?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Kentucky treats autocycles like motorcycles in traffic yet waives both cycle endorsements and helmet mandates.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: What specific danger does loose gravel pose compared with narrow ditch-lined country roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Spotting loose aggregate early prevents skids while watching narrow crests guards against center-hugging oncoming cars.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How do opposing drivers settle priority at a single-lane bridge?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Yielding cleanly when another nose reaches the bridge warning first prevents head-on standoffs.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: What distinct hazards come from steel bridge grates, wooded hills, and uncontrolled rural crossroads?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Slowing ahead of all three rural traps gives your brakes room when visibility or traction drops.
sec11-card-sec11-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Grates skate, hills hide, crossroads surprise

visual_sync.text_span: Grates skate, hills hide, crossroads surprise

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: How do Kentucky traffic duties and licensing-or-helmet rules split for autocycle operators?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Permit questions test that standard operator licenses suffice without motorcycle endorsements or mandatory helmets.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What causes most trailer crashes, and how should cargo weight split front-to-back?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Tail-heavy loading lifts tongue weight off your rear tires and whips the trailer into violent fishtailing.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: How do you calm a swaying trailer right away, and how do you fix the root cause?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes or gassing out of trailer sway amplifies the pendulum swing until the rig jackknifes.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Near what top speed should towed rigs cruise, and when do you brake for hills?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Scrubbing speed before the downgrade starts prevents cooked brakes from fading halfway down the mountain.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How do stopping distances, passing gaps, and cornering paths change when pulling a trailer?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Trailer wheels cut tighter arcs than your bumper and clip curbs or signs on tight turns.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Where does your steering hand go to aim a backing trailer, and how do you fix jackknifing?

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: What pre-trip and fuel-stop habits keep long trailer hauls from ending in roadside breakdowns?

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Which two pedal inputs must you strictly avoid while calming a swaying trailer?

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: What cruising speed ceiling and hill-braking habit fit safe trailer towing?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Heavy combinations push hard downhill, so capping pace and slowing on level crest pavement keeps control.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: What steering adjustments handle inside-cutting trailers on forward turns versus backing maneuvers?

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: What equipment gets checked on walk-arounds, and how should long towing trips be paced?

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Which three crash-avoidance actions serve as every driver's escape tools during a road emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Freezing on one instinct traps new drivers when steering around or accelerating clear would prevent impact.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: How should you brake during a sudden emergency in a car equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Lifting off the pedal when it vibrates or clicks kills anti-lock stopping power right before impact.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which emergency braking method should you follow if your vehicle lacks anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Stomping non-anti-lock pedals locks all four tires into a helpless slide with zero steering response.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What steering sequence lets you swerve around road trouble and safely regain straight control?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Forgetting to counter-steer straight after clearing a hazard launches your car into oncoming traffic or ditches.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Where should your hands stay while driving, and how do you dodge obstacles or darting animals?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Driving one-handed leaves you unable to brake and steer smoothly together when a deer bolts out.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Under what kind of crash threat does speeding up become the safest escape choice?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes when another vehicle charges your rear bumper or side door guarantees a collision.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How does emergency braking in an anti-lock car compare with braking in a non-anti-lock car?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Mixing up anti-lock and conventional braking techniques wastes precious stopping feet when traffic halts abruptly ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does a pure emergency swerve differ from dodging an animal that darts onto the road?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Knowing whether to steer clean around or scrub speed while steering keeps tires planted on pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Which escape tools handle threats ahead versus threats closing in from behind or the side?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Matching your escape move to the direction of danger pulls your vehicle out of the collision zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What three mistakes trigger a skid, and which driver reactions make a slide turn deadly?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Slamming pedals or yanking the wheel violently turns a minor traction loss into a fatal spinout.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What is your first move in a skid, and how do you slow a straight slide with anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Staring at the ditch pulls your hands toward danger instead of guiding tires down open pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How should you slow down during a skid if your vehicle has no anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Hard pedal force freezes non-anti-lock wheels solid so tires skate across wet asphalt like hockey pucks.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: How do you steer out of a sideways rear-wheel skid without whipping into a second slide?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Holding steering lock too long as the nose straightens snaps the tail violently the opposite way.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: How long must you keep working the wheel in a skid, and which control matters most?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Giving up after one correction lets residual fishtailing whip your vehicle sideways across adjacent lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: How do you safely return to the road after your tires drop off the pavement edge?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Yanking back onto high asphalt at highway speed catches the pavement lip and slingshots you oncoming.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How does braking inside a skid differ between anti-lock vehicles and plain-brake vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Pumping anti-lock brakes or stomping plain ones ruins tire grip right when control hangs by threads.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: What two-step steering rhythm pulls a car cleanly out of a sideways skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Late unwinding is the classic learner mistake that turns one saved slide into a worse counter-skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What must you do immediately after any crash in Kentucky, and where do non-injury wrecks go?

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Which driver, vehicle, insurance, and scene details should you record after a collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Missing plate numbers, insurer phones, or damage photos leaves you unprotected when repair claims get disputed.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What are your legal duties if you bump an unattended parked car and cannot find the owner?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Driving off without leaving full contact details, plate numbers, and timestamps turns a scrape into hit-and-run.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: When must you file a civilian crash report with Kentucky State Police, and what is the deadline?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Skipping the ten-day filing on uninvestigated wrecks above five hundred dollars risks administrative license trouble.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: How should you care for injured crash victims, and when is moving someone permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Moving an injured passenger without a life-threatening hazard can turn a survivable spine injury into paralysis.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What reasonable aid duties does Kentucky law place on every driver involved in a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Failing to stop, check injuries, or arrange needed medical care brings severe criminal penalties in Kentucky.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: How does handling an injury crash scene differ from handling a non-injury crash in Kentucky?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Knowing when to preserve the scene versus clear travel lanes protects both victims and approaching traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: How does information exchange in a two-driver crash differ from hitting an empty parked car?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Both collisions demand full accountability whether another motorist stands beside you or returns hours later.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Which two ways can a civilian collision report be submitted, and when do you skip filing?

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Under what sole condition may crash victims be moved instead of waiting blanketed for medics?

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How do you prevent mechanical breakdowns, and which dashboard warning lamp demands stopping right away?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Rolling past a lit brake warning lamp gambles every upcoming intersection on failing hydraulic pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: How should you apply the parking brake if your main foot brakes fail while rolling?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Yanking the parking brake hard locks the rear tires instantly and spins a brakeless car sideways.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What last-resort steps stop your vehicle if both main brakes and parking brake fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Cutting engine power sheds speed so you can guide the car onto a safe off-road stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: How does steering pull differ between a front-tire blowout and a rear-tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Recognizing whether the nose pulls sharply or the tail shakes keeps you from panicking into barriers.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What should your hands and feet do the instant a tire blows out at speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Stomping the brake on a shredded tire pitches weight onto the rim and flips control away.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Where should you stop to change a blown tire, and what warning lights go on?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Changing a flat inside an active travel lane invites distracted highway traffic right into your back.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: How do you steer and brake to safety when your engine stalls while moving?

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Once a stalled vehicle stops off the road, what steps do you take if restarting fails?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: A raised hood and four-way flashers signal distress early so passing motorists give wide clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What sequence safely stops your car if the accelerator sticks down while driving?

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: Where should you park a disabled vehicle, and which two blind road spots are forbidden?

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: How far behind a broken-down car do warning flares belong, and whom should you phone?

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: In what exact order do you use backup stopping methods when your main brakes fail?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Dragging the parking brake preserves full steering assist before you resort to shutting the engine down.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: How can you tell a front-tire blowout apart from a rear-tire blowout by feel?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Instant symptom recognition keeps both hands anchored straight instead of jerking against a blown tire.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: How does your first move for a dead engine differ from a stuck runaway accelerator?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Stalled engines already lost thrust while stuck throttles need power cut and neutral before gentle braking.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Which road features must disabled cars avoid, and how far back should flares sit?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Clear sightlines plus two hundred to three hundred feet of flare warning prevent deadly rear-end strikes.
